title.zh: 卷一百八十九上 列傳第一百三十九上: 儒學上
title.raw: 卷一百八十九上 列傳第一百三十九上: 儒學上 Volume 189 Biographies 139: Confucian Scholars 1

sentences.zh: 古稱儒學家者流，本出於司徒之官，可以正君臣，明貴賤，美教化，移風俗，莫若於此焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity they called the school of Confucian scholars; it originally issued from the office of the Minister of Education. For correcting lord and minister, clarifying noble and base, beautifying instruction and transformation, and shifting customs and mores, nothing was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The school of Confucian scholars in antiquity traced its origins to the office of Minister of Education. For rectifying the relations between ruler and subject, clarifying rank and status, refining moral instruction, and transforming social customs, nothing surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 故前古哲王，鹹用儒術之士；

translations.literal: Therefore the wise kings of former ages all employed men skilled in Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sage rulers of antiquity all drew on men versed in Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 漢家宰相，無不精通一經。

translations.literal: Among the Han dynasty's chancellors, none failed to master thoroughly one classic.
translations.idiomatic: Not one of the Han chancellors failed to master a single canonical classic.

sentences.zh: 朝廷若有疑事，皆引經決定，由是人識禮教，理致升平。

translations.literal: When the court had doubtful matters, all cited the classics to decide; thereby people knew ritual and teaching, and principle reached elevated peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the court faced doubtful matters, it settled them by appeal to the classics; thus the people came to know ritual and instruction, and order rose toward peace.

sentences.zh: 近代重文輕儒，或參以法律，儒道既喪，淳風大衰，故近理國多劣於前古。

translations.literal: In recent times they valued literary skills and slighted Confucian learning, sometimes mixing in legal statutes; the Confucian Way was already lost, pure customs greatly declined, therefore recent governance of states was mostly inferior to former antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times literary skill was prized and Confucian learning slighted, and legal statutes were sometimes mixed in. With the Way of the Ru lost, simple honesty withered—and recent statecraft has often fallen short of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自隋氏道消，海內版蕩，彜倫攸篸，戎馬生郊，先代之舊章，往聖之遺訓，掃地盡矣！

translations.literal: From the time the Sui dynasty's Way was extinguished, within the seas the land was unsettled, constant principles were scattered, war horses bred at the suburbs, the former ages' old statutes and the past sages' handed-down instructions were all swept clean to the ground!
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui fell and the realm was torn apart, human order collapsed and war horses grazed at the city walls. The statutes of former ages and the teachings of the sages were swept utterly away.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義太原，初定京邑，雖得之馬上，而頗好儒臣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised righteous arms at Taiyuan and first secured the capital, though he had gained it on horseback, he rather favored Confucian ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu raised his standard at Taiyuan and first secured the capital, he had won the throne from the saddle—yet he held Confucian officials in real regard.

sentences.zh: 以義寧三年五月，初令國子學置生七十二員，取三品已上子孫；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yining, he first ordered the Directorate of Education to enroll seventy-two students, drawn from descendants of third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yining 3, he first ordered seventy-two students enrolled at the Directorate of Education, drawn from families of third rank and above.

sentences.zh: 太學置生一百四十員，取五品已上子孫；

translations.literal: The Imperial University enrolled one hundred forty students, drawn from descendants of fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University took one hundred forty students from families of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 四門學生一百三十員，取七品已上子孫。

translations.literal: The Four Gates Academy enrolled one hundred thirty students, drawn from descendants of seventh rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Gates Academy took one hundred thirty students from families of seventh rank and above.

sentences.zh: 上郡學置生六十員，中郡五十員，下郡四十員。

translations.literal: Upper prefecture schools enrolled sixty students, middle prefectures fifty, lower prefectures forty.
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures were allotted sixty students each, middle prefectures fifty, and lower prefectures forty.

sentences.zh: 上縣學並四十員，中縣三十員，下縣二十員。

translations.literal: Upper county schools each forty students, middle counties thirty, lower counties twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Upper counties were allotted forty students each, middle counties thirty, and lower counties twenty.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，詔皇族子孫及功臣子弟，於秘書外省別立小學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, an edict ordered that descendants of the imperial clan and sons of meritorious officials establish a separate elementary school at the Outer Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1, an edict directed that imperial clansmen and the sons of meritorious officials attend a separate elementary school at the Outer Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 盛德必祀，義存方策，達人命世，流慶後昆。

translations.literal: Great virtue must be sacrificed to; righteousness resides in written records; a man who comprehends fate and commands an age leaves blessings flowing to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Great virtue demands sacrifice; righteousness lives on in the written record. A man who grasps the age and shapes his times leaves blessings for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 建國君人，弘風闡教，崇賢彰善，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: Founding a state and ruling the people, spreading the wind and expounding teaching, honoring the worthy and displaying goodness—nothing is loftier than this.
translations.idiomatic: To found a state and govern its people, to spread moral influence and expound instruction, to honor the worthy and make goodness manifest—nothing ranks above this.

sentences.zh: 自八卦初陳，九疇攸敘，徽章互垂，節文不備。

translations.literal: From when the Eight Trigrams were first displayed and the Nine Categories were set in order, emblems and insignia hung one upon another, but regulations and forms were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: From the first display of the Eight Trigrams and the ordering of the Nine Categories, emblems and insignia multiplied—yet ritual forms remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 爰始姬旦，匡翊周邦，創設禮經，尤明典憲。

translations.literal: Then began Ji Dan, who supported and assisted the Zhou state, created and established the ritual classics, and was especially clear in canonical statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Ji Dan, who steadied the Zhou state, established the ritual classics, and above all clarified canonical law.

sentences.zh: 啟生人之耳目，窮法度之本源，化起《二南》，業隆八百；

translations.literal: He opened the ears and eyes of living men, exhausted the root source of law and measure, transformation arose from the Two Souths, and his enterprise flourished for eight hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: He opened men's ears and eyes, traced law and measure to their source, raised transformation from the Two Souths, and built an enterprise that flourished for eight hundred years.

sentences.zh: 豐功茂德，冠於終古。

translations.literal: Abundant achievement and luxuriant virtue crowned all of remote antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His abundant achievement and towering virtue stood above all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 暨乎王道既衰，頌聲不作，諸侯力爭，禮樂陵遲。

translations.literal: When the royal Way had already declined, eulogistic songs were no longer made, feudal lords strove by force, and ritual and music fell into decay.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal Way waned, praise songs ceased, feudal lords fought by force, and ritual and music fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 粵若宣父，天資睿哲；

translations.literal: Then there was the Venerable Ni, heaven-endowed with keen wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the Venerable Ni, endowed by Heaven with keen wisdom.

sentences.zh: 經綸齊、魯之內，揖讓洙、泗之間；

translations.literal: He wove governance within Qi and Lu, bowing and yielding between the Zhu and Si rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He wove order within Qi and Lu, teaching courtesy between the Zhu and Si.

sentences.zh: 綜理遺文，弘宣舊制。

translations.literal: He gathered and ordered surviving texts and broadly proclaimed the old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered surviving texts and broadly restored the old institutions.

sentences.zh: 四科之教，歷代不刊；

translations.literal: The teaching of the four categories was never effaced through successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of the four categories has never been effaced across the ages.

sentences.zh: 三千之文，風流無歇。

translations.literal: The three thousand pieces of writing—its current of influence never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: His three thousand disciples carried his influence forward without end.

sentences.zh: 惟茲二聖，道著群生，守祀不修，明褒尚闕。

translations.literal: Only these two sages—whose Way was manifest to all living beings—yet sacrifice was not maintained and clear honors were still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: These two sages made the Way manifest to all living beings—yet their sacrifices were neglected and fitting honors still lacking.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨區宇，興化崇儒，永言先達，情深紹嗣。

translations.literal: We rule the realm, raise transformation and honor Confucian learning, forever speak of the former worthies, and our feelings run deep to continue their line.
translations.idiomatic: We rule the realm, promote moral transformation and honor Confucian learning, ever mindful of the former worthies, with deep resolve to carry on their line.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司於國子學立周公、孔子廟各一所，四時致祭。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the responsible officials to establish at the Directorate of Education one temple each to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, with sacrifices at the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials establish at the Directorate of Education one temple each to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, with seasonal sacrifices throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 仍博求其後，具以名聞，詳考所宜，當加爵土。

translations.literal: Moreover, broadly seek their descendants, report all names, examine in detail what is fitting, and confer noble rank and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, seek out their descendants far and wide, report their names, examine what is fitting, and confer rank and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 是以學者慕向，儒教聿興。

translations.literal: Therefore scholars turned toward it in admiration, and Confucian teaching thereupon arose.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars turned toward it in admiration, and Confucian teaching flourished anew.

sentences.zh: 至三年，太宗討平東夏，海內無事，乃銳意經籍，於秦府開文學館。

translations.literal: By the third year, Taizong had pacified the eastern Xia and within the seas there was no trouble; he then keenly applied himself to the classics and opened a Literary Academy at the Prince of Qin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year, Emperor Taizong had pacified the east and the realm was at peace; he then turned keenly to the classics and opened a Literary Academy at the Prince of Qin's residence.

sentences.zh: 廣引文學之士，下詔以府屬杜如晦等十八人為學士，給五品珍膳，分為三番更直，宿於閣下。

translations.literal: He broadly recruited men of literary learning, issued an edict appointing eighteen men including the residence staff member Du Ruhui as academicians, granted them fifth-rank delicacies, divided them into three watches for rotation on duty, and lodged them below the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited literary scholars widely, appointed eighteen men including Du Ruhui as academicians by edict, supplied them fifth-rank delicacies, divided them into three watches, and quartered them in the pavilion below.

sentences.zh: 及即位，又於正殿之左，置弘文學館，精選天下文儒之士虞世南、褚亮、姚思廉等，各以本官兼署學士，令更日宿直。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he also placed the Hongwen Literary Academy to the left of the main hall, carefully selecting literary Confucians of the realm such as Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Yao Silian, each holding his original office while additionally serving as academician, ordered to lodge on duty in daily rotation.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he established the Hongwen Literary Academy to the left of the main hall, carefully selecting literary Confucians such as Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Yao Silian, each retaining his regular post while serving as academician on rotating night duty.

sentences.zh: 聽朝之暇，引入內殿，講論經義，商略政事，或至夜分乃罷。

translations.literal: In leisure from hearing court, he brought them into the inner hall to discuss the meaning of the classics and deliberate on government affairs, sometimes not dismissing until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals from court he summoned them to the inner hall to discuss the classics and deliberate on affairs of state, sometimes not dismissing them until midnight.

sentences.zh: 又召勛賢三品已上子孫，為弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He also summoned descendants of meritorious worthies of third rank and above to serve as Hongwen Academy students.
translations.idiomatic: He also enrolled descendants of meritorious officials of third rank and above as Hongwen Academy students.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，停以周公為先聖，始立孔子廟堂於國學，以宣父為先聖，顏子為先師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, he ceased taking the Duke of Zhou as supreme sage, first established Confucius's temple hall at the Directorate of Learning, took the Venerable Ni as supreme sage, and Yanzi as supreme teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 he ceased honoring the Duke of Zhou as supreme sage, established Confucius's temple at the Directorate of Learning, named the Venerable Ni supreme sage and Yan Hui supreme teacher.

sentences.zh: 大征天下儒士，以為學官。

translations.literal: He greatly recruited Confucian scholars of the realm to serve as learning officials.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Confucian scholars from across the realm to serve as learning officials.

sentences.zh: 數幸國學，令祭酒、博士講論。

translations.literal: He repeatedly visited the Directorate of Learning and ordered the chancellor of education and erudites to lecture and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly visited the Directorate of Learning and ordered the chancellor and erudites to lecture.

sentences.zh: 畢，賜以束帛。

translations.literal: When finished, he bestowed bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When they finished, he bestowed bundles of silk.

sentences.zh: 學生能通一大經已上，鹹得署吏。

translations.literal: Students who could master one great classic or more were all permitted to be appointed clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Students who mastered at least one of the great classics were all eligible for clerkly appointment.

sentences.zh: 又於國學增築學舍一千二百間，太學、四門博士亦增置生員，其書算合置博士、學生，以備藝文，凡三千二百六十員。

translations.literal: He also at the Directorate of Learning added twelve hundred schoolrooms; the Imperial University and Four Gates erudites also increased enrolled students; for writing and calculation together he established erudites and students to complete the arts and letters—in all three thousand two hundred sixty persons.
translations.idiomatic: He added twelve hundred schoolrooms at the Directorate of Learning, increased enrollment at the Imperial University and Four Gates, and established erudites and students in writing and calculation to complete the arts—in all 3,260 persons.

sentences.zh: 其玄武門屯營飛騎，亦給博士，授以經業；

translations.literal: The Xuanwu Gate garrison flying cavalry were also supplied erudites and taught the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The flying cavalry of the Xuanwu Gate garrison were also assigned erudites and taught the classics.

sentences.zh: 有能通經者，聽之貢舉。

translations.literal: Those who could master the classics were permitted to be presented for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Those who mastered the classics were permitted to enter the examination system.

sentences.zh: 是時四方儒士，多抱負典籍，雲會京師。

translations.literal: At this time Confucian scholars from the four directions, many bearing classics on their backs, gathered like clouds at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars from every quarter, many bearing classics on their backs, gathered like clouds at the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄而高麗及百濟、新羅、高昌、吐蕃等諸國酋長，亦遣子弟請入於國學之內。

translations.literal: Before long the chieftains of Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, Tubo, and other states also sent their sons and younger brothers to request entry within the Directorate of Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the chieftains of Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, Tibet, and other states also sent their sons to study at the Directorate of Learning.

sentences.zh: 鼓篋而升講筵者，八千余人。

translations.literal: Those who struck their book-cases and ascended to the lecture mat numbered more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight thousand students carried their book-cases to the lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 濟濟洋洋焉，儒學之盛，古昔未之有也。

translations.literal: Grand and abundant indeed—the flourishing of Confucian learning, such as antiquity had never had.
translations.idiomatic: Grand and abundant indeed—never had Confucian learning flourished so.

sentences.zh: 太宗又以經籍去聖久遠，文字多訛謬，詔前中書侍郎顏師古考定《五經》，頒於天下，命學者習焉。

translations.literal: Taizong also, because the classics had been distant from the sages for long, and the characters had many errors, ordered the former Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu to collate and fix the Five Classics, promulgate them throughout the realm, and command scholars to study them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also found the classics distant from the sages and full of textual errors; he ordered the former Vice Director Yan Shigu to collate the Five Classics, promulgate them throughout the realm, and command scholars to study them.

sentences.zh: 又以儒學多門，章句繁雜，詔國子祭酒孔穎達與諸儒撰定《五經》義疏，凡一百七十卷，名曰《五經正義》，令天下傳習。

translations.literal: Also, because Confucian learning had many schools and chapter-and-verse commentary was complex and tangled, he ordered Chancellor of the Directorate Kong Yingda together with the various Confucians to compile exegeses of the Five Classics—in all one hundred seventy juan, entitled Correct Meaning of the Five Classics—and commanded the realm to transmit and study them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Confucian learning had many schools and commentary had grown tangled, he ordered Chancellor Kong Yingda and other scholars to compile exegeses of the Five Classics—170 juan in all, entitled Correct Meaning of the Five Classics—and commanded the realm to study them.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔曰：「梁皇侃、褚仲都，周熊安生、沈重，陳沈文阿、周弘正、張譏，隋何妥、劉炫等，並前代名儒，經術可紀。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict said: 'Liang Huang Kan and Chu Zhongdu, Zhou Xiong Ansheng and Shen Chong, Chen Shen Wena, Zhou Hongzheng, and Zhang Ji, Sui He Tuo and Liu Xuan, and others—all were famous Confucians of former ages, whose classic learning is worthy of record.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, an edict proclaimed: 'Huang Kan and Chu Zhongdu of Liang, Xiong Ansheng and Shen Chong of Zhou, Shen Wena, Zhou Hongzheng, and Zhang Ji of Chen, He Tuo and Liu Xuan of Sui—these were all famous Confucians of former ages whose classic learning is worthy of record.

sentences.zh: 加以所在學徒，多行其疏，宜加優異，以勸後生。

translations.literal: Moreover, students everywhere mostly practiced their commentaries; they should receive added favor to encourage later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, students everywhere chiefly studied their commentaries; they should receive special favor to encourage later generations.

sentences.zh: 可訪其子孫見在者，錄名奏聞，當加引擢。」

translations.literal: Their living descendants may be sought out, names recorded and reported, and promotion and elevation granted.'
translations.idiomatic: Seek out their living descendants, record their names and report them, and grant promotion and elevation.'

sentences.zh: 二十一年，又詔曰：「左丘明、卜子夏、公羊高、谷梁赤、伏勝、高堂生、戴聖、毛萇、孔安國、劉向、鄭眾、杜子春、馬融、盧植、鄭玄、服虔、何休、王肅、王弼、杜元凱、範寧等二十一人，並用其書，垂於國胄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, another edict said: 'Zuo Qiuming, Bu Zixia, Gongsun Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Gaotang Sheng, Dai Sheng, Mao Chang, Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, Zheng Zhong, Du Zichun, Ma Rong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, He Xiu, Wang Su, Wang Bi, Du Yu, Fan Ning, and twenty-one others—all used their books, handed down to the national heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, another edict proclaimed: 'Zuo Qiuming, Bu Zixia, Gongsun Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Gaotang Sheng, Dai Sheng, Mao Chang, Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, Zheng Zhong, Du Zichun, Ma Rong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, He Xiu, Wang Su, Wang Bi, Du Yu, Fan Ning—these twenty-one men all used their books, handed down to the national heir.

sentences.zh: 既行其道，理合褒崇。

translations.literal: Since their Way was practiced, it was fitting in principle to honor and exalt them.
translations.idiomatic: Since their Way was practiced, it was only fitting to honor them.

sentences.zh: 自今有事太學，可與顏子俱配享孔子廟堂。」

translations.literal: From now on, when there are ceremonies at the Imperial University, they may together with Yanzi be associated in sacrifice at Confucius's temple hall.'
translations.idiomatic: From now on, at Imperial University ceremonies they may share sacrifice in Confucius's temple together with Yan Hui.'

sentences.zh: 其尊重儒道如此。

translations.literal: Such was his respect for the Confucian Way.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his respect for the Confucian Way.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，政教漸衰，薄於儒術，尤重文吏。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, government and teaching gradually declined; he was sparing toward Confucian learning and especially valued literary clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, government and teaching gradually declined; he slighted Confucian learning and especially valued literary clerks.

sentences.zh: 於是醇醲日去，畢競日彰，猶火銷膏而莫之覺也。

translations.literal: Thereupon pure richness daily departed and complete competition daily manifested, like fire consuming fat and none perceiving it.
translations.idiomatic: Pure learning daily waned and ruthless competition daily waxed, like fire consuming tallow—yet none perceived it.

sentences.zh: 及則天稱制，以權道臨下，不吝官爵，取悅當時。

translations.literal: When Zetian assumed regency, she ruled the people by expedient power, was not sparing of offices and ranks, and sought to please the present age.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed regency, she governed by expedient power, lavished offices and ranks without stint, and sought to please the age.

sentences.zh: 其國子祭酒，多授諸王及駙馬都尉，準貞觀舊事。

translations.literal: The chancellors of the Directorate of Education were mostly granted to imperial princes and commandants of cavalry escorting the emperor's son-in-law, following the Zhenguan old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellorship of the Directorate was mostly granted to imperial princes and sons-in-law of the emperor, following Zhenguan precedent.

sentences.zh: 祭酒孔穎達等赴上日，皆講《五經》題。

translations.literal: When chancellors such as Kong Yingda attended on audience days, all lectured on topics from the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: When chancellors such as Kong Yingda attended on audience days, all lectured on topics from the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 至是，諸王與駙馬赴上，唯判祥瑞按三道而已。

translations.literal: By this time, when princes and sons-in-law attended on audience, they only judged auspicious omens according to three categories.
translations.idiomatic: By this time, when princes and sons-in-law attended on audience, they merely judged auspicious omens in three categories.

sentences.zh: 至於博士、助教，唯有學官之名，多非儒雅之實。

translations.literal: As for erudites and assistant instructors, they had only the names of learning officials; most were not truly refined and elegant in substance.
translations.idiomatic: As for erudites and assistant instructors, they bore only the titles of learning officials; most lacked true scholarly substance.

sentences.zh: 是時復將親祠明堂及南郊，又拜洛，封嵩嶽，將取弘文國子生充齊郎行事，皆令出身放選，前後不可勝數。

translations.literal: At this time she was again about to sacrifice in person at the Bright Hall and the southern suburb, also worship at Luo, and enfeoff Mount Song; she intended to take Hongwen and Directorate students to serve as ritual attendants, all granting initial appointment and release for selection—before and after, they could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: She was again about to sacrifice in person at the Bright Hall and southern suburb, worship at Luo, and enfeoff Mount Song; she took Hongwen and Directorate students as ritual attendants, granting them all initial appointment and release for selection—countless in number.

sentences.zh: 因是生徒不復以經學為意，唯茍希僥幸。

translations.literal: Because of this, students no longer took classic learning to heart and only hoped for lucky chance.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, students no longer took classic learning to heart and only hoped for lucky advancement.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，學校頓時隳廢矣。

translations.literal: Within twenty years, the schools suddenly collapsed and were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty years, the schools collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，親幸太學，大開講論，學官生徒，各賜束帛。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, he personally visited the Imperial University, greatly opened lectures and discussions, and bestowed bundles of silk on learning officials and students alike.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Xuanzong personally visited the Imperial University, opened wide lectures and discussion, and bestowed bundles of silk on officials and students alike.

sentences.zh: 及即位，數詔州縣及百官薦舉經通之士。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he repeatedly ordered prefectures, counties, and all officials to recommend men who had mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he repeatedly ordered prefectures, counties, and officials to recommend men who had mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 又置集賢院，招集學者校選，募儒士及博涉著實之流。

translations.literal: He also established the Jixian Academy, recruited and gathered scholars for collation and selection, and enlisted Confucian scholars and those broadly versed and solid in accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also established the Jixian Academy, gathered scholars for collation and selection, and enlisted Confucian scholars and men of broad and solid learning.

sentences.zh: 以為《儒學篇》。

translations.literal: This constitutes the 'Treatise on Confucian Learning.'
translations.idiomatic: This constitutes the 'Treatise on Confucian Learning.'

sentences.zh: 徐文遠，洛州偃師人，陳司空孝嗣玄孫，其先自東海徙家焉。

translations.literal: Xu Wenyuan was a man of Yanshi in Luozhou, a great-great-grandson of Chen Minister of Works Xiao Si; his ancestors had moved their household there from Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenyuan was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou, a great-great-grandson of Chen Minister of Works Xiao Si; his ancestors had moved there from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父徹，梁秘書郎，尚元帝女安昌公主而生文遠。

translations.literal: His father Che was a Liang Secretariat clerk; he married Emperor Yuan's daughter Princess Anchang and begot Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Che was a Liang Secretariat clerk who married Emperor Yuan's daughter Princess Anchang and fathered Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 屬江陵陷，被虜於長安，家貧無以自給。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he was taken captive to Chang'an; the family was poor and had no means to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he was taken captive to Chang'an; the family was too poor to support itself.

sentences.zh: 其兄休，鬻書為事，文遠日閱書於肆，博覽《五經》，尤精《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xiu made a living selling books; Wenyuan daily perused books at the shop, broadly read the Five Classics, and was especially expert in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xiu sold books for a living; Wenyuan spent his days reading in the shop, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially expert in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 時有大儒沈重講於太學，聽者常千余人。

translations.literal: At the time the great Confucian Shen Chong lectured at the Imperial University, and listeners often numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the great Confucian Shen Chong lectured at the Imperial University before audiences often exceeding a thousand.

sentences.zh: 文遠就質問，數日便去。

translations.literal: Wenyuan went to question him and left after only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan went to question him and left after only a few days.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「何辭去之速？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: 'Why did you take leave so quickly?'
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: 'Why did you leave so quickly?'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「觀其所說，悉是紙上語耳，仆皆先已誦得之。

translations.literal: He answered: 'What I observed him saying was all merely words on paper; I had already recited and obtained them all beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'Everything he said was merely words on paper—I had already recited it all myself.

sentences.zh: 至於奧賾之境，翻似未見。」

translations.literal: As for the hidden and profound realm, it rather seemed he had not seen it.'
translations.idiomatic: As for the hidden depths, he seemed never to have reached them.'

sentences.zh: 有以其言告重者，重呼與議論，十余反，重甚嘆服之。

translations.literal: Someone reported his words to Shen Chong; Chong summoned him to debate, and after more than ten exchanges Chong greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported his words to Shen Chong, who summoned him to debate; after more than ten exchanges Chong sighed in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 文遠方正純厚，有儒者風。

translations.literal: Wenyuan was upright, pure, and thick, with the bearing of a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was upright, sincere, and steadfast, with the bearing of a true Confucian.

sentences.zh: 竇威、楊玄感、李密皆從其受學。

translations.literal: Dou Wei, Yang Xuangang, and Li Mi all received learning from him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei, Yang Xuangang, and Li Mi all studied under him.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，累遷太學博士。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, he was repeatedly promoted to erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he rose repeatedly to erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 詔令往并州，為漢王諒講《孝經》、《禮記》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to go to Bingzhou to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites for Prince of Han Liang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to Bingzhou to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites for Prince Liang of Han.

sentences.zh: 及諒反，除名。

translations.literal: When Liang rebelled, he was struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rebelled, Wenyuan was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 大業初，禮部侍郎許善心舉文遠與包愷、褚徽、陸德明、魯達為學官，遂擢授文遠國子博士，愷等並為太學博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shansin recommended Wenyuan together with Bao Kai, Chu Hui, Lu Deming, and Lu Da as learning officials; Wenyuan was thereupon promoted and appointed erudite of the Directorate, while Kai and the others were all appointed erudites of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye, Vice Minister Xu Shansin recommended Wenyuan together with Bao Kai, Chu Hui, Lu Deming, and Lu Da as learning officials; Wenyuan was appointed erudite of the Directorate, and the others erudites of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時人稱文遠之《左氏》、褚徽之《禮》、魯達之《詩》、陸德明之《易》，皆為一時之最。

translations.literal: People of the time called Wenyuan's Zuo Commentary, Chu Hui's Rites, Lu Da's Odes, and Lu Deming's Changes all the foremost of their age.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries ranked Wenyuan's Zuo Commentary, Chu Hui's Rites, Lu Da's Odes, and Lu Deming's Changes as the finest of the age.

sentences.zh: 文遠所講釋，多立新義，先儒異論，皆定其是非，然後詰駁諸家，又出己意，博而且辨，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: In Wenyuan's lectures and exegeses he often established new meanings; he settled right and wrong in the differing opinions of former Confucians, then examined and refuted the various schools, and again brought forth his own ideas—broad and yet discriminating, so listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In his lectures Wenyuan often established new interpretations, settled the rights and wrongs of earlier scholars' disputes, then examined and refuted rival schools and advanced his own views—broad yet discriminating, so that listeners forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 後越王侗署為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Yue Tong appointed him chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Tong of Yue appointed him chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽饑饉，文遠出城樵采，為李密軍所執。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang suffered famine; Wenyuan went outside the city to gather firewood and was seized by Li Mi's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang suffered famine, Wenyuan went outside the city to gather firewood and was seized by Li Mi's army.

sentences.zh: 密令文遠南面坐，備弟子禮北面拜之。

translations.literal: Mi ordered Wenyuan to sit facing south and, with the full ceremony of a disciple, bowed to him facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Mi seated Wenyuan facing south and, with the full ceremony of a disciple, bowed to him facing north.

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「老夫疇昔之日，幸以先王之道，仰授將軍。

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: 'In former days this old man was fortunate to impart to the general, looking up, the Way of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan said: 'In former days I was fortunate enough to impart to you, General, the Way of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 時經興替，倏焉已久。

translations.literal: Time has passed through rise and fall; suddenly it has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties have risen and fallen; how long it has been.

sentences.zh: 今將軍屬風雲之際，為義眾所歸，權鎮萬物，威加四海，猶能屈體弘尊師之義，此將軍之德也，老夫之幸也！

translations.literal: Now the general belongs to a time of wind and clouds, is followed by righteous multitudes, holds authority over the ten thousand things, and his might extends over the four seas—yet you can still humble your person and magnify the meaning of honoring the teacher. This is the general's virtue and this old man's good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Now you stand at a turning point in history, followed by righteous multitudes, holding authority over all things, your might extending across the four seas—yet you can still humble yourself and honor your teacher. This is your virtue, General, and my good fortune!

sentences.zh: 既荷茲厚禮，安不盡言乎！

translations.literal: Having received this generous courtesy, how could I not speak my utmost!
translations.idiomatic: Having received such generous courtesy, how could I not speak my mind fully!

sentences.zh: 但未審將軍意耳！

translations.literal: But I have not yet examined the general's intent!
translations.idiomatic: But I do not yet know your intent, General!

sentences.zh: 欲為伊、霍繼絕扶傾，雖遲暮，猶願盡力；

translations.literal: If you wish to be like Yi Yin and Huo Guang, continuing the cut-off line and supporting the leaning, though I am in late old age, I still wish to exert my utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to be like Yi Yin and Huo Guang, restoring a broken line and supporting a tottering throne, though I am in my dotage I will still exert my utmost.

sentences.zh: 若為莽、卓乘危迫險，則老夫耄矣，無能為也。」

translations.literal: If you would be like Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo, seizing danger and pressing peril, then this old man is already in extreme old age and can do nothing.'
translations.idiomatic: If you would be like Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo, seizing power in crisis and pressing peril, then this old man is too feeble to help.'

sentences.zh: 密頓首曰：「昨奉朝命，垂拜上公，冀竭庸虛，匡奉國難。

translations.literal: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: 'Yesterday I received the court's command and was granted the title of Grand Duke, hoping to exhaust my mediocre emptiness and support the state's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: 'Yesterday I received the court's command and was granted the title of Grand Duke, hoping to exhaust my poor abilities in support of the state's peril.

sentences.zh: 所以未朝見者，不測城內人情。

translations.literal: The reason I have not yet attended court audience is that I cannot gauge the sentiments of people within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have not yet presented myself at court is that I cannot gauge the mood within the city.

sentences.zh: 且欲先征化及，報復冤恥，立功贖罪，然後凱旋，入拜天闕。

translations.literal: Moreover I wish first to campaign against Huaji, avenge grievous wrongs, establish merit to redeem guilt, and then return in triumph to bow at the heavenly gate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I wish first to campaign against Huaji, avenge this grievous wrong, win merit to redeem my guilt, and then return in triumph to bow at the imperial gate.

sentences.zh: 此密之本意，惟先生教之。」

translations.literal: This is Mi's fundamental intent; I ask only that the master instruct me.'
translations.idiomatic: This is my true intent, Master—I ask only for your guidance.'

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「將軍名臣之子，累顯忠節，前受誤於玄感，遂乃暫墜家聲。

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: 'The general is the son of a famous minister; you have repeatedly displayed loyalty and integrity. Formerly you were misled by Xuangang, and thus for a time your family's reputation fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan said: 'You are the son of a famous minister and have repeatedly shown loyalty and integrity. You were once misled by Yang Xuangang and for a time your family's reputation suffered.

sentences.zh: 行迷未遠，而回車復路，終於忠孝，用康家國，天下之人，是所望於將軍也。」

translations.literal: You had not gone far astray before you turned your carriage and returned to the road, ending in loyalty and filial piety to bring peace to family and state—the people of the realm place their hopes in the general for this.'
translations.idiomatic: You had not gone far astray before you turned back, and if you end in loyalty and filial piety to bring peace to family and state, that is what the people of the realm hope for from you, General.'

sentences.zh: 密又頓首曰：「敬聞命矣，請奉以周旋。」

translations.literal: Mi again bowed his head to the ground and said: 'I have respectfully heard your command; I beg to follow it in all my dealings.'
translations.idiomatic: Mi bowed his head again and said: 'I have heard your command with respect; I shall follow it in all my dealings.'

sentences.zh: 及征化及還，而王世充已殺元文都等，權兵專制。

translations.literal: When he returned from campaigning against Huaji, Wang Shichong had already killed Yuan Wendu and others and monopolized military power.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from campaigning against Huaji, Wang Shichong had already killed Yuan Wendu and others and seized sole control of the army.

sentences.zh: 密又問計於文遠，答曰：「王世充亦門人也，頗得識之。

translations.literal: Mi again asked Wenyuan for counsel; he answered: 'Wang Shichong was also a student of mine, and I came to know him fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Mi again asked Wenyuan for counsel; he answered: 'Wang Shichong was also my student, and I know him fairly well.

sentences.zh: 是人殘忍，意又褊促，既乘此勢，必有異圖。

translations.literal: This man is cruel, and his mind is also narrow and urgent; having seized this momentum, he is certain to harbor a different design.
translations.idiomatic: He is cruel and narrow-minded; having seized this momentum, he is certain to harbor designs of his own.

sentences.zh: 將軍前計為不諧矣，非破王世充，不可朝覲。」

translations.literal: The general's former plan will not succeed; unless Wang Shichong is defeated, you cannot attend court audience.'
translations.idiomatic: Your former plan will not succeed, General; unless you defeat Wang Shichong, you cannot present yourself at court.'

sentences.zh: 密曰：「嘗謂先生儒者，不學軍旅之事，今籌大計，殊有明略。」

translations.literal: Mi said: 'I once thought the master was a Confucian who did not study military affairs; now in planning great strategy you show exceptional clarity of design.'
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: 'I once thought you were a Confucian who knew nothing of military affairs; yet in planning great strategy you show exceptional clarity.'

sentences.zh: 及密敗，復入東都，王世充給其廩食，而文遠盡敬，見之先拜。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Wenyuan again entered the Eastern Capital; Wang Shichong supplied his grain rations, yet Wenyuan showed full respect and bowed first upon seeing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Wenyuan returned to the Eastern Capital; Wang Shichong supplied his grain, yet Wenyuan showed him full respect and bowed first whenever they met.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「聞君踞見李密，而敬王公，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: 'I heard you sat with legs spread when you saw Li Mi, yet you respect Prince Wang—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: 'I heard you sat informally when you met Li Mi, yet you show respect to Prince Wang—why?'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「李密，君子也，能受酈生之揖；

translations.literal: He answered: 'Li Mi is a gentleman and could accept Li Yiji's bow.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'Li Mi is a gentleman and could accept Li Yiji's informal bow.

sentences.zh: 王公，小人也，有殺故人之義。

translations.literal: Prince Wang is a petty man and has the righteousness of killing old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wang is a petty man who kills his old associates.

sentences.zh: 相時而動，豈不然歟！」

translations.literal: One acts according to the times—is it not so!'
translations.idiomatic: One acts according to the times—is that not so!'

sentences.zh: 後王世充僭號，復以為國子博士。

translations.literal: Later, when Wang Shichong usurped the title, he again appointed him erudite of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, he again appointed Wenyuan erudite of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 因出樵采，為羅士信獲之，送於京師，復授國子博士。

translations.literal: Once when he went out to gather firewood he was seized by Luo Shixin, sent to the capital, and again appointed erudite of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went out to gather firewood he was seized by Luo Shixin, sent to the capital, and again appointed erudite of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，高祖幸國學，觀釋奠，遣文遠發《春秋》題，諸儒設難蜂起，隨方占對，皆莫能屈。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude, Gaozu visited the Directorate of Learning to observe the libation sacrifice, sent Wenyuan to pose a topic from the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the various Confucians raised challenges like swarming bees; he responded according to each direction, and none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 6, Emperor Gaozu visited the Directorate of Learning for the libation sacrifice, had Wenyuan pose a topic from the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the assembled scholars raised challenges from every side; he answered each in turn, and none could best him.

sentences.zh: 封東莞縣男。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Dongguan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Dongguan County.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，卒官。

translations.literal: At age seventy-four he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 撰《左傳音》三卷、《義疏》六十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Pronunciation of the Zuo Commentary in three juan and Exegesis and Commentary in sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Pronunciation of the Zuo Commentary in three juan and Exegesis and Commentary in sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 孫有功，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Yougong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yougong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 陸德明，蘇州吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Deming was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Deming was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 初受學於周弘正，善言玄理。

translations.literal: He first received learning from Zhou Hongzheng and was skilled in discussing arcane principles.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied under Zhou Hongzheng and was skilled in discussing arcane philosophy.

sentences.zh: 陳大建中，太子征四方名儒，講於承先殿。

translations.literal: During Chen Dajian, the crown prince summoned famous Confucians from the four directions to lecture at Chengxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chen Dajian reign, the crown prince summoned famous Confucians from across the realm to lecture at Chengxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 德明年始弱冠，往參焉。

translations.literal: Deming was just reaching the capping age and went to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Deming had just reached his capping age and went to take part.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒徐克開講，恃貴縱辨，眾莫敢當；

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Directorate Xu Ke opened the lecture, relying on his noble status to debate freely; none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xu Ke opened the lecture, relying on his noble rank to debate freely; none dared contend with him.

sentences.zh: 德明獨與抗對，合朝賞嘆。

translations.literal: Deming alone contended against him, and the whole court admired and sighed in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Deming alone contended against him, and the whole court marveled.

sentences.zh: 解褐始興王國左常侍，遷國子助教。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the common cloth he became Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Shixing and was transferred to assistant instructor of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Shixing and was transferred to assistant instructor of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝嗣位，以為秘書學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui succeeded to the throne, Deming was appointed Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 大業中，廣召經明之士，四方至者甚眾。

translations.literal: During Daye he broadly summoned men clear in the classics; very many arrived from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye he broadly summoned men eminent in the classics, and very many arrived from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 遣德明與魯達、孔褒俱會門下省，共相交難，無出其右者。

translations.literal: He sent Deming together with Lu Da and Kong Bao to meet at the Secretariat Chancellery, where they mutually debated and challenged one another, and none surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Deming together with Lu Da and Kong Bao to the Secretariat Chancellery to debate one another, and none could surpass them.

sentences.zh: 授國子助教。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant instructor of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant instructor of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，封其子為漢王，署德明為師，就其家，將行束脩之禮。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he enfeoffed his son as King of Han, appointed Deming as his teacher, came to his home, and was about to perform the ceremony of presenting dried meat as tuition.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, he enfeoffed his son as King of Han, appointed Deming as his teacher, came to Deming's home, and was about to perform the ceremony of presenting dried meat as tuition.

sentences.zh: 德明恥之，因服巴豆散，臥東壁下。

translations.literal: Deming was shamed by this and therefore took croton powder, lying down beneath the east wall.
translations.idiomatic: Deming was shamed by this and took croton powder, lying down beneath the east wall.

sentences.zh: 王世充子入，跪床前，對之遺痢，竟不與語。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's son entered, knelt before the bed, and facing him suffered diarrhea; Deming would not speak with him at all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's son entered and knelt before the bed; Deming faced him and relieved himself, and would not speak a word.

sentences.zh: 遂移病於成臯，杜絕人事。

translations.literal: He thereupon feigned illness at Chenggao and cut off all human contact.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon feigned illness at Chenggao and cut off all contact with the world.

sentences.zh: 王世充平，太宗征為秦府文學館學士，命中山王承乾從其受業。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, Taizong summoned him as an academician of the Prince of Qin's Literary Academy and ordered Prince of Zhongshan Chengqian to receive learning from him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong was defeated, Taizong summoned him as an academician of the Prince of Qin's Literary Academy and ordered Prince Chengqian of Zhongshan to study under him.

sentences.zh: 尋補太學博士。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 後高祖親臨釋奠，時徐文遠講《孝經》，沙門惠乘講《波若經》，道士劉進喜講《老子》，德明難此三人，各因宗指，隨端立義，眾皆為之屈。

translations.literal: Later Gaozu personally attended the libation sacrifice; at the time Xu Wenyuan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the monk Huicheng lectured on the Prajna Sutra, and the Daoist Liu Jinxi lectured on the Laozi. Deming challenged these three men, each according to his school's aim establishing meaning as the occasion required, and the assembly all yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Gaozu personally attended the libation sacrifice; Xu Wenyuan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the monk Huicheng on the Prajna Sutra, and the Daoist Liu Jinxi on the Laozi. Deming challenged all three, establishing his arguments according to each school's principles, and the assembly yielded to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之，賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved of this and bestowed fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was pleased and bestowed fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，拜國子博士，封吳縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed erudite of the Directorate and enfeoffed as Baron of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed erudite of the Directorate and enfeoffed as Baron of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 撰《經典釋文》三十卷、《老子疏》十五卷、《易疏》二十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Exegesis of the Classics in thirty juan, Commentary on the Laozi in fifteen juan, and Commentary on the Changes in twenty juan, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Exegesis of the Classics in thirty juan, Commentary on the Laozi in fifteen juan, and Commentary on the Changes in twenty juan, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 太宗後嘗閱德明《經典釋文》，甚嘉之，賜其家束帛二百段。

translations.literal: Taizong later once perused Deming's Exegesis of the Classics, greatly approved of it, and bestowed on his family two hundred bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong later read Deming's Exegesis of the Classics, greatly admired it, and bestowed two hundred bundles of silk on his family.

sentences.zh: 子敦信，龍朔中官至左侍極，同東西臺三品。

translations.literal: His son Dunxin, during Longshuo, reached the office of Left Attendant-at-Court, third rank equal to the Eastern and Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dunxin, during Longshuo, rose to Left Attendant-at-Court, third rank equal to the Eastern and Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 曹憲，揚州江都人也。

translations.literal: Cao Xian was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xian was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為秘書學士。

translations.literal: He served Sui as Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 每聚徒教授，諸生數百人。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered disciples to teach, his students numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he gathered disciples to teach, his students numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 當時公卿已下，亦多從之受業。

translations.literal: At the time, from dukes and ministers downward, many also received learning from him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials, from dukes and ministers downward, also studied under him.

sentences.zh: 憲又精諸家文字之書，自漢代杜林、衛宏之後，古文泯絕，由憲，此學復興。

translations.literal: Xian was also expert in the various schools' books on characters; from the Han dynasty's Du Lin and Wei Hong onward, ancient script had been extinguished, and through Xian this learning revived.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was also expert in paleography; since Du Lin and Wei Hong of Han, ancient script had been lost, and through Xian the study was revived.

sentences.zh: 大業中，煬帝令與諸學者撰《桂苑珠叢》一百卷，時人稱其該博。

translations.literal: During Daye, Emperor Yang ordered him together with various scholars to compile the Cassia Garden Pearl Collection in one hundred juan; people of the time praised its comprehensiveness and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye, Emperor Yang ordered him and other scholars to compile the Cassia Garden Pearl Collection in one hundred juan; contemporaries praised its comprehensiveness.

sentences.zh: 憲又訓註張揖所撰《博雅》，分為十卷，煬帝令藏於秘閣。

translations.literal: Xian also glossed and annotated Zhang Yi's Broad Ready Reference, dividing it into ten juan; Emperor Yang ordered it stored in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also glossed Zhang Yi's Broad Ready Reference, dividing it into ten juan; Emperor Yang ordered it stored in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，揚州長史李襲譽表薦之，太宗征為弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Yangzhou Chief Administrator Li Xiyu memorialized recommending him, and Taizong summoned him as Hongwen Academy academician.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, Yangzhou Chief Administrator Li Xiyu recommended him by memorial, and Taizong summoned him as Hongwen Academy academician.

sentences.zh: 以年老不仕，乃遣使就家拜朝散大夫，學者榮之。

translations.literal: Because of old age he did not take office; an envoy was sent to his home to appoint him Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age he declined office; the court sent an envoy to his home to appoint him Grand Master of Palace Leisure, which scholars regarded as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 太宗又嘗讀書有難字，字書所闕者，錄以問憲，憲皆為之音訓及引證明白，太宗甚奇之。

translations.literal: Taizong also once, when reading and encountering difficult characters omitted from character books, recorded them to ask Xian; Xian provided pronunciation and glosses and clear citations for all, and Taizong greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also once, when reading and encountering difficult characters omitted from dictionaries, recorded them to ask Xian; Xian provided pronunciation, glosses, and clear citations for all, and Taizong greatly marveled.

sentences.zh: 年一百五歲卒。

translations.literal: He died at age one hundred five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of one hundred and five.

sentences.zh: 所撰《文選音義》，甚為當時所重。

translations.literal: His compiled Pronunciation and Meaning of the Literary Selection was greatly valued by the time.
translations.idiomatic: His Pronunciation and Meaning of the Literary Selection was greatly valued in his day.

sentences.zh: 初，江、淮間為《文選》學者，本之於憲，又有許淹、李善、公孫羅復相繼以《文選》教授，由是其學大興於代。

translations.literal: Initially, scholars of the Literary Selection between the Yangtze and Huai took Xian as their foundation; moreover Xu Yan, Li Shan, and Gongsun Luo in succession taught the Literary Selection, and thereby this learning greatly flourished in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, scholars of the Literary Selection in the Yangtze-Huai region took Xian as their foundation; Xu Yan, Li Shan, and Gongsun Luo in turn taught the Literary Selection, and thereby the study flourished greatly in the age.

sentences.zh: 許淹者，潤州句容人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yan was a man of Jurong in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan was a native of Jurong in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 少出家為僧，後又還俗。

translations.literal: In youth he left home to become a monk, and later returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he became a monk, and later returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 博物洽聞，尤精詁訓。

translations.literal: Broad in things and comprehensive in hearing, he was especially expert in glossing and exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and well informed, he was especially expert in glossing and exegesis.

sentences.zh: 撰《文選音》十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Pronunciation of the Literary Selection in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Pronunciation of the Literary Selection in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 李善者，揚州江都人。

translations.literal: Li Shan was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 方雅清勁，有士君子之風。

translations.literal: Upright, refined, clear, and forceful, he had the bearing of a gentleman and scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, refined, and forceful, he had the bearing of a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 明慶中，累補太子內率府錄事參軍、崇賢館直學士，兼沛王侍讀。

translations.literal: During Mingqing he was repeatedly appointed Recording Secretary of the Crown Prince's Inner Rate Office, direct academician of the Chongxian Academy, and concurrently Reader-in-Waiting to the Prince of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingqing he rose to Recording Secretary of the Crown Prince's Inner Rate Office, direct academician of the Chongxian Academy, and Reader-in-Waiting to the Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 嘗註解《文選》，分為六十卷，表上之。

translations.literal: He once annotated the Literary Selection, dividing it into sixty juan, and memorialized it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Literary Selection in sixty juan and presented it to the throne by memorial.

sentences.zh: 賜絹一百二十匹，詔藏於秘閣。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred twenty bolts of silk, and an edict ordered it stored in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred twenty bolts of silk, and an edict ordered the work stored in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 除潞王府記室參軍，轉秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary of the Prince of Lu's residence and transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary of the Prince of Lu's residence and transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 乾封中，出為經城令。

translations.literal: During Qianfeng he went out to serve as magistrate of Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianfeng he was sent out to serve as magistrate of Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 坐與賀蘭敏之周密，配流姚州。

translations.literal: Because of close association with Helan Minzhi, he was sentenced to exile in Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his close association with Helan Minzhi, he was sentenced to exile in Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦得還，以教授為業，諸生多自遠方而至。

translations.literal: Later he met an amnesty and was able to return, making teaching his profession; many students came from distant places.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was pardoned and returned, making teaching his profession; many students came from distant places.

sentences.zh: 又撰《漢書辯惑》三十卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled Resolving Doubts on the Han History in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Resolving Doubts on the Han History in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 載初元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Zaichu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zaichu.

sentences.zh: 子邕，亦知名。

translations.literal: His son Yong was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong was also well known.

sentences.zh: 公孫羅，江都人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Luo was a man of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Luo was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 歷沛王府參軍，無錫縣丞。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer of the Prince of Pei's residence and as assistant magistrate of Wuxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of the Prince of Pei's residence and as assistant magistrate of Wuxi County.

sentences.zh: 撰《文選音義》十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Pronunciation and Meaning of the Literary Selection in ten juan, circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Pronunciation and Meaning of the Literary Selection in ten juan, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 詢初學王羲之書，後更漸變其體，筆力險勁，為一時之絕。

translations.literal: Xun at first studied Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, then gradually transformed his style; his brush strength was perilous and forceful, unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun at first studied Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, then gradually developed his own style; his brushwork was perilous and forceful, unmatched in his age.

sentences.zh: 人得其尺牘文字，鹹以為楷範焉。

translations.literal: When people obtained even a foot of his writing, all took it as a model standard.
translations.idiomatic: When people obtained even a scrap of his writing, all took it as the standard model.

sentences.zh: 高麗甚重其書，嘗遣使求之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo greatly valued his writing and once sent envoys to request it.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo greatly valued his calligraphy and once sent envoys to request samples.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘆曰：「不意詢之書名，遠播夷狄，彼觀其跡，固謂其形魁梧耶！」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed and said: 'I did not expect Xun's fame in calligraphy to spread far among the barbarians; when they see his traces, they surely suppose his form is tall and imposing!'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed and said: 'I did not expect Xun's fame as a calligrapher to reach the barbarians; when they see his writing, they must suppose he is tall and imposing!'

sentences.zh: 武德七年，詔與裴矩、陳叔達撰《藝文類聚》一百卷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, an edict ordered him together with Pei Ju and Chen Shuda to compile the Literary Arts Classified Collection in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7, an edict ordered him together with Pei Ju and Chen Shuda to compile the Literary Arts Classified Collection in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 奏之，賜帛二百段。

translations.literal: They presented it and were granted two hundred sections of silk.
translations.idiomatic: They presented it and were granted two hundred sections of silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，官至太子率更令、弘文館學士，封渤海縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he reached the offices of Crown Prince's Director of Water Clocks and Hongwen Academy academician, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he rose to Crown Prince's Director of Water Clocks and Hongwen Academy academician, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 年八十余卒。

translations.literal: He died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 子通，少孤，母徐氏教其父書。

translations.literal: His son Tong, orphaned in youth, was taught his father's calligraphy by his mother, Lady Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong, orphaned in youth, was taught his father's calligraphy by his mother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 每遺通錢，紿云：「質汝父書跡之直。」

translations.literal: Whenever she gave Tong money, she deceived him, saying: 'This is the price for pawning your father's calligraphic traces.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she gave Tong money, she told him: 'This is payment for your father's calligraphy.'

sentences.zh: 通慕名甚銳，晝夜精力無倦，遂亞於詢。

translations.literal: Tong's desire for fame was very keen; day and night his energy never tired, and he came to rank just below Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's ambition burned fiercely; day and night he never tired, and he came to rank just below his father.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Yifeng he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: During Yifeng he rose repeatedly to Secretariat Drafting Official.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning beyond the prescribed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning beyond the prescribed ritual.

sentences.zh: 起復本官，每入朝，必徒跣至皇城門外。

translations.literal: Recalled to his former office, whenever he entered court he always went barefoot to outside the imperial city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to his former office, whenever he entered court he went barefoot to the gate of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 直宿在省，則席地藉槁。

translations.literal: When on night duty at the Secretariat, he spread matting on the ground and used straw for bedding.
translations.idiomatic: When on night duty at the Secretariat, he slept on the ground on straw.

sentences.zh: 非公事不言，亦未嘗啟齒。

translations.literal: He spoke nothing except on public business and never opened his teeth otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke only on public business and otherwise never opened his mouth.

sentences.zh: 歸家必衣缞绖，號慟無恆。

translations.literal: Returning home he always wore hemp mourning garments and wailed without constancy.
translations.idiomatic: At home he always wore hemp mourning garments and wailed without cease.

sentences.zh: 自武德已來，起復後而能哀戚合禮者，無與通比。

translations.literal: From Wude onward, among those recalled to office who could observe grief and sorrow in accord with ritual, none could be compared with Tong.
translations.idiomatic: From Wude onward, among those recalled to office who observed grief in accord with ritual, none could compare with Tong.

sentences.zh: 年兇未葬，四年居廬不釋服，家人冬月密以氈絮置所眠席下，通覺，大怒，遽令徹之。

translations.literal: The year was ill-starred and the burial had not yet taken place; for four years he dwelt in the mourning hut without removing his garments. In winter his family secretly placed felt padding beneath his sleeping mat; Tong noticed, grew greatly angry, and immediately ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: The year was ill-starred and the burial had not yet taken place; for four years he dwelt in the mourning hut without removing his garments. In winter his family secretly placed felt padding beneath his sleeping mat; Tong noticed, flew into a rage, and immediately ordered it removed.

sentences.zh: 五遷，垂拱中至殿中監，賜爵渤海子。

translations.literal: After five promotions, during Chuigong he reached Director of the Palace Bureau and was granted the title Viscount of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions, during Chuigong he rose to Director of the Palace Bureau and was granted the title Viscount of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 天授元年，封夏官尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshou, he was enfeoffed as Minister of the Summer Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianshou era, he was appointed Minister of the Summer Office.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉司禮卿，判納言事。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Minister of Rites and concurrently discharged the duties of Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was transferred to Minister of Rites and assigned to handle the responsibilities of the Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 為相月余，會鳳閣舍人張嘉福等請立武承嗣為皇太子，通與岑長倩固執以為不可，遂忤諸武意，為酷吏所陷，被誅。

translations.literal: Having served as chancellor for little more than a month, when Fengge Attendant Zhang Jiafu and others requested that Wu Chengsi be established as heir apparent, Tong together with Cen Changqian stubbornly held that it could not be done; thereby he offended the Wu faction, was framed by cruel officials, and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as chief minister for little more than a month, when Fengge Attendant Zhang Jiafu and others petitioned to install Wu Chengsi as crown prince, Tong and Cen Changqian steadfastly opposed it; he thereby provoked the Wu clan, was ensnared by the cruel officials, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, his offices and enfeoffments were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era, his official ranks and titles were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 硃子奢，蘇州吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Zishe was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zishe was a native of Wu district in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從鄉人顧彪習《春秋左氏傳》，後博觀子史，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals under fellow townsman Gu Biao; later he broadly read the various masters and histories and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals under his fellow townsman Gu Biao; he later read widely in the philosophers and histories and excelled at polished prose.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，直秘書學士。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he served as Attending Secretary Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye period, he served as an attending academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及天下大亂，辭職歸鄉里，尋附於杜伏威。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into great disorder, he resigned his office and returned to his home district; shortly thereafter he attached himself to Du Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into widespread chaos, he resigned and returned home, soon afterward joining Du Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，隨伏威入朝，授國子助教。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, following Fuwei in presenting himself at court, he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, he accompanied Fuwei to court and was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，高麗、百濟同伐新羅，連兵數年不解，新羅遣使告急。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Goguryeo and Baekje together attacked Silla; warfare continued for several years without resolution, and Silla sent envoys in urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign, Goguryeo and Baekje jointly attacked Silla; hostilities dragged on for years, and Silla sent envoys pleading for help.

sentences.zh: 乃假子奢員外散騎侍郎充使，喻可以釋三國之憾，雅有儀觀，東夷大欽敬之，三國王皆上表謝罪，賜遣甚厚。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zishe was provisionally appointed Supernumerary Gentlemen-Attendant-in-Ordinary as envoy, instructing them that the grievances of the three states could be released; he possessed refined bearing and appearance, and the eastern barbarians greatly admired and respected him; the kings of all three states submitted memorials of apology, and the gifts and send-offs were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe was then appointed supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and dispatched as envoy, explaining how the three kingdoms might settle their grievances. Possessing an elegant bearing, he won great admiration among the eastern peoples; all three kings submitted memorials of apology, and the court lavished generous gifts upon his departure.

sentences.zh: 初，子奢之出使也，太宗謂曰：「海夷頗重學問，卿為大國使，必勿藉其束脩，為之講說。

translations.literal: When Zishe first set out on his mission, Taizong said to him: 'The maritime barbarians greatly value learning; as envoy of a great state, you must by no means rely on their customary gifts and should lecture them instead.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zishe departed on his mission, Taizong told him: 'The maritime peoples greatly esteem learning. As envoy of a great power, you must not accept their customary tribute-gifts—instead, lecture them.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，當以中書舍人待卿。」

translations.literal: If on your return the mission accords with my intent, you shall be treated with the rank of Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: If your mission wins my approval upon your return, I shall appoint you Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 子奢至其國，欲悅夷虜之情，遂為發《春秋左傳》題，又納其美女之贈。

translations.literal: When Zishe reached their country, wishing to please the barbarians' feelings, he thereupon lectured on topics from the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and also accepted their gift of beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to please the foreigners, Zishe lectured on the Zuo Commentary and also accepted their gift of beautiful women.

sentences.zh: 使還，太宗責其違旨，猶惜其才，不至深譴，令散官直國子學。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission, Taizong blamed him for defying his instructions; still cherishing his talent, he did not go so far as severe punishment, but ordered him to serve at the Imperial University as an unattached official.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Taizong reproached him for disobeying his orders; still valuing his talent, the emperor stopped short of severe punishment and assigned him to the Imperial University as an unattached official.

sentences.zh: 轉諫議大夫、弘文館學士，遷國子司業，仍為學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and Academician of the Hongwen Hall, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial University, and still served as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief censor and Hongwen Hall academician, then appointed vice director of the Imperial University while retaining his academician post.

sentences.zh: 子奢風流蘊藉，頗滑稽，又輔之以文義，由是數蒙宴遇，或使論難於前。

translations.literal: Zishe was refined and cultured, quite witty and humorous, and further aided by literary learning; thereby he repeatedly received invitations to banquets, and at times was made to debate difficult points before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured, witty, and learned, Zishe was repeatedly invited to imperial banquets and sometimes called upon to debate difficult questions before the throne.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 張士衡，瀛州樂壽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiheng was a native of Leshou in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiheng was a native of Leshou in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父之慶，齊國子助教。

translations.literal: His father Zhang Zhiqing served as Assistant Instructor of the Qi Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Zhiqing served as assistant instructor at the Qi Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 士衡九歲喪母，哀慕過禮。

translations.literal: At nine years of age Shiheng lost his mother; his grief and longing exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of nine Shiheng lost his mother; his grief and devotion exceeded what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 父友齊國博士劉軌思見之，每為掩泣。

translations.literal: When his father's friend, Qi State University Erudite Liu Guisi, saw him, he would each time cover his face and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his father's friend Liu Guisi, erudite of the Qi Imperial University, saw him, he would cover his face and weep.

sentences.zh: 謂其父曰：「昔伯饒號『張曾子』，亦豈能遠過！

translations.literal: He said to his father: 'In former times Bo Rao was called "Zhang the Second Zengzi"—can he really have been far surpassed!
translations.idiomatic: He said to Shiheng's father: 'In former times Bo Rao was called "Zhang the Second Zengzi"—surely he cannot have been far surpassed!

sentences.zh: 吾聞君子不親教，當為成就之。」

translations.literal: I have heard that a gentleman does not instruct his own child directly; one ought to bring him to accomplishment.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a gentleman does not teach his own son personally; one should see to his full development.'

sentences.zh: 及長，軌思授以《毛詩》、《周禮》，又從熊安生及劉焯受《禮記》，皆精究大義。

translations.literal: When grown, Guisi instructed him in the Mao Odes and the Rites of Zhou, and he further studied the Record of Rites under Xiong Ansheng and Liu Zhuo, penetrating thoroughly the great principles in each.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, Guisi taught him the Mao Odes and the Rites of Zhou, and he further studied the Record of Rites under Xiong Ansheng and Liu Zhuo, mastering the essential principles of each.

sentences.zh: 此後遍講《五經》，尤攻《三禮》。

translations.literal: After this he lectured broadly on the Five Classics, especially concentrating on the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he lectured widely on the Five Classics, with particular concentration on the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為余杭令，後以年老歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He served Sui as magistrate of Yuhang; later, due to old age, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as magistrate of Yuhang; later, in his old age, he retired to his home district.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，幽州都督、燕王靈夔備玄纁束帛之禮，就家迎聘，北面師之。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Youzhou Military Commissioner and Prince of Yan Ling Cai prepared the ritual gifts of dark and scarlet silks and went to his home to invite and employ him, treating him as teacher with north-facing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, Youzhou military commissioner and Prince of Yan Ling Cai prepared the ceremonial gifts of dark and scarlet silks, came to his home to invite him, and honored him as his teacher with the ceremony due a master.

sentences.zh: 庶人承乾在東宮，又加旌命。

translations.literal: The commoner Chenggan, when at the Eastern Palace, also bestowed further marks of honor upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the commoner Chenggan was at the Eastern Palace, he too issued further honors to him.

sentences.zh: 及至洛陽宮謁見，太宗延之升殿，賜食，擢授朝散大夫、崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: When he came to Luoyang Palace for audience, Taizong had him ascend the hall, bestowed food, and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience at Luoyang Palace, Taizong invited him up to the hall, offered him a meal, and promoted him to grand master of splendid happiness and academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 承乾見之，問以齊氏滅亡之由緒，對曰：「齊後主悖虐無度，昵近小人。

translations.literal: Chenggan upon seeing him asked about the causes and course of the Qi dynasty's destruction; he replied: 'The Later Lord of Qi was perverse and cruel without measure and intimate with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggan met him, he asked about the reasons for the Qi dynasty's fall. Shiheng replied: 'The last ruler of Qi was wantonly cruel and drew close to petty men.

sentences.zh: 至如高阿那瑰、駱提婆、韓長鸞等，皆奴仆下才，兇險無賴，是信是使，以為心腹。

translations.literal: As for Gao Ana'gui, Luo Tipo, Han Changluan, and the like—all were men of servile and low talent, fierce, dangerous, and unscrupulous—he trusted and employed them as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Gao Ana'gui, Luo Tipo, and Han Changluan were all of servile and base ability, vicious and reckless; yet he trusted them utterly and made them his closest advisers.

sentences.zh: 誅害忠良，疏忌骨肉。

translations.literal: He slaughtered the loyal and good and estranged and suspected his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the loyal and worthy and alienated his own kin.

sentences.zh: 窮極奢靡，剝喪黎元。

translations.literal: He pursued luxury to the extreme and stripped and ruined the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged in extravagance to the utmost and plundered the common people.

sentences.zh: 所以周師臨郊，人莫為用，以至覆滅，實此之由。」

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhou armies reached the suburbs, no man would fight for him, leading to utter destruction—the truth of it lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Zhou armies reached the capital's outskirts, no one would fight for him, and the state was destroyed—this was the true cause.

sentences.zh: 承乾又問曰：「布施營功德，有果報不？」

translations.literal: Chenggan asked again: 'Does giving alms and performing meritorious deeds bring karmic retribution?'
translations.idiomatic: Chenggan asked again: 'Does giving alms and performing meritorious deeds bring karmic reward?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事佛在於清凈無欲，仁恕為心。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Serving the Buddha lies in purity and freedom from desire, with benevolence and forbearance in the heart.
