translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'Devotion to Buddhism consists in purity and freedom from desire, with benevolence and forbearance at heart.

sentences.zh: 如其貪婪無厭，驕虐是務，雖復傾財事佛，無救目前之禍。

translations.literal: If one is instead insatiably greedy and devoted to arrogance and cruelty, though one pour out one's wealth in Buddhist service, it cannot save one from present calamity.
translations.idiomatic: But if one is insatiably greedy and devoted to arrogance and cruelty, then even pouring out one's wealth in service to Buddhism cannot avert present disaster.

sentences.zh: 且善惡之報，若影隨形，此是儒書之言，豈徒佛經所說。

translations.literal: Moreover, the retribution of good and evil follows like a shadow follows a form—this is the teaching of Confucian books, not merely what Buddhist sutras say.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reward for good and evil follows like a shadow follows a body—this is taught in Confucian texts, not only in Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 是為人君父，當須仁慈；

translations.literal: Therefore as ruler and father one ought to be benevolent;
translations.idiomatic: As ruler and father, one must be benevolent;

sentences.zh: 為人臣子，宜盡忠孝。

translations.literal: as minister and son one ought to fulfill loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: as minister and son, one must be loyal and filial.

sentences.zh: 仁慈忠孝，則福祚攸永；

translations.literal: Benevolence, loyalty, and filial piety—then fortune and position endure;
translations.idiomatic: With benevolence, loyalty, and filial piety, fortune and rank endure;

sentences.zh: 如或反此，則殃禍斯及。

translations.literal: if one reverses this, then disaster and calamity overtake one.
translations.idiomatic: but if one does the opposite, disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 此理昭然，願殿下勿為憂慮。」

translations.literal: This principle is evident; I pray Your Highness not be troubled by worry.'
translations.idiomatic: This principle is clear; I urge Your Highness not to worry.'

sentences.zh: 及承乾廢黜，敕給乘傳，令歸本鄉。

translations.literal: When Chenggan was deposed and degraded, an edict granted him relay transport and ordered him to return to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggan was deposed, an edict granted him relay transport and ordered him to return to his native district.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 士衡既禮學為優，當時受其業擅名於時者，唯賈公彥為最焉。

translations.literal: Since Shiheng excelled in ritual learning, of those who received his instruction and won renown at the time, Jia Gongyan alone stood foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shiheng excelled in ritual studies, of those who studied under him and won fame in their day, Jia Gongyan alone stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 賈公彥，洺州永年人。

translations.literal: Jia Gongyan was a native of Yongnian in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Gongyan was a native of Yongnian in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，官至太學博士。

translations.literal: During Yonghui he reached the post of Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign he rose to the post of erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 撰《周禮義疏》五十卷、《儀禮義疏》四十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled fifty juan of Exegetical Commentary on the Rites of Zhou and forty juan of Exegetical Commentary on the Ceremonial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled fifty fascicles of Exegetical Commentary on the Rites of Zhou and forty fascicles of Exegetical Commentary on the Ceremonial Rites.

sentences.zh: 子大隱，官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Dayin rose to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dayin rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時有趙州李玄植，又受《三禮》於公彥，撰《三禮音義》行於代。

translations.literal: At that time there was Li Xuanzhi of Zhaozhou, who further received instruction in the Three Rites from Gongyan and compiled Phonetic and Semantic Notes on the Three Rites, which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xuanzhi of Zhaozhou also studied the Three Rites under Gongyan and compiled Phonetic and Semantic Notes on the Three Rites, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 玄植兼習《春秋左氏傳》於王德韶，受《毛詩》於齊威，博涉漢史及老、莊諸子之說。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi also studied the Zuo Commentary under Wang Deshao, received the Mao Odes from Qi Wei, and broadly penetrated Han histories and the doctrines of Laozi, Zhuangzi, and various masters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi also studied the Zuo Commentary under Wang Deshao and the Mao Odes under Qi Wei, and read widely in Han histories and the teachings of Laozi, Zhuangzi, and other philosophers.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷太子文學、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Literary Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he was repeatedly promoted to literary tutor of the heir apparent and direct academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，屢被召見。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong he was repeatedly summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was repeatedly summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 與道士、沙門在御前講說經義，玄植辨論甚美，申規諷，帝深禮之。

translations.literal: Together with Daoist priests and Buddhist monks he expounded scripture before the throne; Xuanzhi's disputation was very elegant, and in offering remonstrance and admonition the emperor deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Along with Daoist priests and Buddhist monks he expounded the classics before the throne; Xuanzhi's discourse was eloquent, and in offering remonstrance and admonition he won the emperor's deep respect.

sentences.zh: 後坐事左遷汜水令，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in an affair, he was demoted to magistrate of Sishui and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, implicated in an offense, he was demoted to magistrate of Sishui and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 張後胤，蘇州昆山人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Houyin was a native of Kunshan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Houyin was a native of Kunshan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父中，有儒學，隋漢王諒出牧并州，引為博士。

translations.literal: His father Zhang Zhong was learned in Confucian studies; when Sui Prince of Han Yang Liang went out to govern Bingzhou, he was invited as Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Zhong was a Confucian scholar; when the Sui Prince of Han, Yang Liang, was sent to govern Bingzhou, he was invited to serve as erudite.

sentences.zh: 後胤從父在并州，以學行見稱。

translations.literal: Houyin accompanied his father to Bingzhou and was acclaimed for his learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Houyin accompanied his father to Bingzhou and was praised for his scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 時高祖鎮太原，引居賓館。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan and invited him to reside in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan and invited him to stay at his residence.

sentences.zh: 太宗就受《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: The Taizong (then Prince of Qin) came to him to receive instruction in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The future Taizong came to him to study the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 武德中，累除燕王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: During Wude he was repeatedly appointed Consultation and Planning Staff Officer to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign he was repeatedly appointed consultation and planning officer to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，後胤上言：「陛下昔在太原，問臣：『隋氏運終，何族當得天下？』

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Houyin submitted a memorial: 'Your Majesty formerly at Taiyuan asked me: "The Sui mandate is ending—which clan shall obtain the realm under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, Houyin submitted a memorial: 'Your Majesty, when you were at Taiyuan, once asked me: "The Sui mandate is ending—which clan will win the empire?

sentences.zh: 臣奉對：『李姓必得。

translations.literal: I respectfully replied: "The Li surname shall surely obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully answered: "The house of Li will surely prevail."

sentences.zh: 公家德業，天下系心，若於此首謀，長驅關右，以圖帝業，孰不幸賴！』

translations.literal: Your household's virtue and achievements have captured the hearts of the realm; if at this juncture you take the lead in plotting, drive straight through to the Pass and west, and aim at the imperial enterprise—who would not consider himself fortunate to rely upon you!
translations.idiomatic: Your family's virtue and accomplishments have won the hearts of the realm. If you take the lead now, march swiftly into the Guan region, and set your sights on the imperial throne—who would not count himself fortunate to follow you!

sentences.zh: 此實微臣早識天命。」

translations.literal: This was truly this humble subject's early recognition of Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: That was truly this humble subject's early recognition of Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「此事並記之耳。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: 'This affair is all recorded, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: 'That matter is all on record—that is all.'

sentences.zh: 因詔入賜宴，言及平昔，從容謂曰：「今弟子何如？」

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned him in and bestowed a banquet; speaking of former days, he said leisurely: 'How are your disciples today?'
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Houyin to court and gave him a banquet; recalling old times, he said casually: 'How are your disciples today?'

sentences.zh: 後胤對曰：「昔孔子領徒三千，達者無子男之位。

translations.literal: Houyin replied: 'Formerly Confucius led three thousand disciples, yet among those who attained success none held the rank of viscount or baron.
translations.idiomatic: Houyin replied: 'In antiquity Confucius led three thousand disciples, yet not one of those who achieved distinction held a noble rank.

sentences.zh: 臣翼贊一人，為萬乘主，計臣功逾於先聖。」

translations.literal: I assisted a single man who became master of ten thousand chariots; reckoned by my achievement, I surpass the former sage.'
translations.idiomatic: I assisted a single man who became emperor; by that measure, my achievement surpasses that of the ancient sage.'

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悅，賜良馬五匹，拜燕王府司馬。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased, bestowed five fine horses, and appointed him Director of the Prince of Yan's household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased, bestowed five fine horses on him, and appointed him director of the Prince of Yan's household.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，轉散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial University and transferred to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chancellor of the Imperial University and then transferred to regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，請致仕，加金紫光祿大夫，給賜並同職事。

translations.literal: Early in Yonghui he requested retirement; he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with stipends and gifts equal to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign he requested retirement; he was granted the additional title of grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, with stipends and perquisites equal to his former office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部侍郎，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously appointed vice minister of rites and granted burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 蓋文達，冀州信都人也。

translations.literal: Gai Wenda was a native of Xindu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wenda was a native of Xindu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，尤明《三傳》。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered the classics and histories, especially proficient in the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and was especially accomplished in the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 性方雅，美須貌，有士君子之風。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and refined; he had a handsome beard and countenance and possessed the bearing of a gentleman and scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and refined in character, with a handsome beard and bearing, he had the air of a true gentleman-scholar.

sentences.zh: 刺史竇抗嘗廣集儒生，令相問難，其大儒劉焯、劉軌思、孔穎達鹹在坐，文達亦參焉。

translations.literal: Prefect Dou Kang once broadly gathered Confucian scholars and had them question and challenge one another; the great scholars Liu Zhuo, Liu Guisi, and Kong Yingda were all seated, and Wenda also participated.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Dou Kang once gathered a large assembly of Confucian scholars for mutual debate; the eminent scholars Liu Zhuo, Liu Guisi, and Kong Yingda were all present, and Wenda took part as well.

sentences.zh: 既論難，皆出諸儒意表，抗大奇之，問曰：「蓋生就誰受學？」

translations.literal: When the debate was concluded, all exceeded the other scholars' expectations; Kang was greatly astonished and asked: 'Student Gai, under whom did you receive instruction?
translations.idiomatic: When the debate ended, his answers surpassed what the other scholars had expected; Kang was astonished and asked: 'Master Gai, under whom did you study?

sentences.zh: 劉焯對曰：「此生岐嶷，出自天然。

translations.literal: Liu Zhuo replied: 'This student is precocious and gifted by nature itself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuo answered: 'This young man is precocious—his gifts come from nature itself.

sentences.zh: 以多問寡，焯為師首。」

translations.literal: When the many question the few, Zhuo serves as chief teacher.'
translations.idiomatic: When the many question the few, Zhuo is merely the nominal teacher.'

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「可謂冰生於水而寒於水也。」

translations.literal: Kang said: 'One may say ice is born of water yet colder than water.'
translations.idiomatic: Kang said: 'One might say that ice is born of water yet colder than water.'

sentences.zh: 武德中，累授國子助教。

translations.literal: During Wude he was repeatedly appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign he was repeatedly appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 太宗在籓，召為文學館直學士。

translations.literal: When Taizong was still a prince, he was summoned as Direct Academician of the Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was still a prince, he was summoned to serve as direct academician of the Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，遷諫議大夫，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Hongwen Hall Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to chief censor and concurrent Hongwen Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除國子司業。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed vice director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 俄拜蜀王師，以王有罪，坐免。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Preceptor to the Prince of Shu; because the prince was guilty, he was implicated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed preceptor to the Prince of Shu; when the prince was found guilty, Wenda was implicated and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 其宗人文懿，亦以儒業知名，當時稱為「二蓋」焉。

translations.literal: His clansman Wenyi was also famed for Confucian learning; at the time they were called 'the two Gais.'
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wenyi was also renowned for Confucian scholarship; contemporaries called them 'the two Gais.'

sentences.zh: 文懿者，貝州宋城人也。

translations.literal: Wenyi was a native of Songcheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi was a native of Songcheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 武德初，歷國子助教。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he served as Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he served as assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時高祖別於秘書省置學，教授王公之子，時以文懿為博士。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu separately established a school within the Secretariat to instruct the sons of princes and dukes, and at the time Wenyi served as Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu established a separate school within the Secretariat to instruct the sons of princes and dukes, and Wenyi served as its erudite.

sentences.zh: 文懿嘗開講《毛詩》，發題，公卿鹹萃，更相問難，文懿發揚風雅，甚得詩人之致。

translations.literal: Wenyi once opened lecture on the Mao Odes, proposing topics; the high ministers all gathered, questioning and challenging one another in turn; Wenyi expounded the elegant and classical style and very much captured the spirit of the poets.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi once lectured on the Mao Odes, proposing topics for discussion; high officials all gathered and questioned one another in turn; Wenyi expounded the elegant style of the classics and captured the true spirit of the poets.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，卒於國子博士。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he died while serving as Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he died while serving as erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 谷那律，魏州昌樂人也。

translations.literal: Gu Nalu was a native of Changle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Nalu was a native of Changle in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累補國子博士。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly appointed to fill the post of Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he was repeatedly appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎褚遂良稱為「九經庫」。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Huangmen, Chu Suiliang, called him 'the storehouse of the Nine Classics.'
translations.idiomatic: Huangmen vice director Chu Suiliang called him 'the storehouse of the Nine Classics.'

sentences.zh: 尋遷諫議大夫，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Hongwen Hall Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to chief censor and concurrent Hongwen Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太宗出獵，在途遇雨，因問：「油衣若為得不漏？」

translations.literal: Once he accompanied Taizong on a hunt; on the road they met rain, and [Taizong] therefore asked: 'How can an oilskin coat be made not to leak?
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied Emperor Taizong on a hunt. Rain fell on the road, and the emperor asked, 'How can you make an oilskin raincoat that does not leak?

sentences.zh: 那律曰：「能以瓦為之，必不漏矣。」

translations.literal: Nalu said: 'If one can make it of tile, it certainly will not leak.'
translations.idiomatic: Nalu replied, 'Make it of tile, and it will never leak.'

sentences.zh: 意欲太宗不為畋獵。

translations.literal: His intent was that Taizong not go hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to dissuade Taizong from hunting.

sentences.zh: 太宗悅，賜帛二百段。

translations.literal: Taizong was pleased and bestowed two hundred bales of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was delighted and rewarded him with two hundred bales of silk.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yonghui reign he died in office.

sentences.zh: 蕭德言，雍州長安人，齊尚書左僕射思話玄孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Deyan was a native of Chang'an in Yongzhou, a great-great-grandson of Xiao Sihua, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Deyan was a native of Chang'an in Yong Prefecture and a great-great-grandson of Xiao Sihua, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 本蘭陵人，陳亡，徙關中。

translations.literal: Originally he was a man of Lanling; when Chen perished, he moved to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally from Lanling; after the fall of Chen they resettled in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 祖介，梁侍中、都官尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jie was attendant-in-ordinary and Director of Punishments of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jie had served Liang as attendant-in-ordinary and director of punishments.

sentences.zh: 父引，陳吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yin was vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had been vice minister of personnel under Chen.

sentences.zh: 並有名於時。

translations.literal: All were famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Each had been eminent in his day.

sentences.zh: 德言博涉經史，尤精《春秋左氏傳》，好屬文。

translations.literal: Deyan was broadly versed in the classics and histories, especially expert in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Deyan ranged widely through the classics and histories, excelled above all in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and loved to write.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，除著作郎，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was appointed Master of Writings and concurrently Hongwen Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he was appointed master of writings and concurrent academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 德言晚年尤篤誌於學，自晝達夜，略無休倦。

translations.literal: In his later years Deyan was especially devoted in will to learning, from day through night, almost without rest or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Deyan pursued learning with exceptional zeal, studying from dawn to night with scarcely a pause.

sentences.zh: 每欲開《五經》，必束帶盥濯，危坐對之。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to open the Five Classics, he would gird his sash, wash, and sit upright facing them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he opened the Five Classics he girded his sash, washed his hands, and sat upright before them.

sentences.zh: 妻子候間請曰：「終日如是，無乃勞乎？」

translations.literal: His wife, waiting at the interval, asked: 'All day like this—might it not be laborious?
translations.idiomatic: His wife, watching from the doorway, asked, 'To go on like this all day—is it not exhausting?

sentences.zh: 德言曰：「敬先聖之言，豈憚如此！」

translations.literal: Deyan said: 'To revere the words of the former sages—how could one shrink from this!'
translations.idiomatic: Deyan answered, 'These are the words of the ancient sages. How could I begrudge the effort!'

sentences.zh: 時高宗為晉王，詔德言授經講業。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozong was Prince of Jin; an edict ordered Deyan to deliver the classics and lecture on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Gaozong was Prince of Jin, and an edict appointed Deyan to instruct him in the classics.

sentences.zh: 及升春宮，仍兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When he ascended the Eastern Palace, [Deyan] still concurrently served as lecture companion.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Deyan continued as his reading tutor.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老，請致仕，太宗不許。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of age, he requested retirement; Taizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing his age, he asked to retire; Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 又遺之書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent him a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent him a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 朕歷觀前代，詳覽儒林，至於顏、閔之才，不終其壽；

translations.literal: I have surveyed former ages in turn and reviewed the forest of scholars in detail; as for the talents of Yan and Min, they did not complete their years;
translations.idiomatic: I have looked back through the ages and studied the annals of scholars. Talents like Yan Hui and Min Sun did not live out their span;

sentences.zh: 遊、夏之德，不逮其學。

translations.literal: the virtue of You and Xia did not measure up to their learning.
translations.idiomatic: men like Ziyou and Zixia fell short of their own learning in virtue.

sentences.zh: 惟卿幼挺珪璋，早標美譽。

translations.literal: Only you, from youth upright as jade and scepter-stone, early marked with fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: You alone, from youth, stood like jade and scepter-stone, and won an early name for excellence.

sentences.zh: 下帷閉戶，包括《六經》；

translations.literal: Drawing curtains, closing doors, you encompassed the Six Classics;
translations.idiomatic: Behind drawn curtains and closed doors you mastered the Six Classics;

sentences.zh: 映雪聚螢，牢籠百氏。

translations.literal: reading by snow-reflected light, gathering fireflies, you mastered all the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: studied by snowlight and firefly glow, and took in the whole world of learning.

sentences.zh: 自隋季版蕩，阇序無聞，儒道墜泥塗，《詩書》填坑穽。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of the Sui's end, school gates went unheard of; the Confucian Way fell into mud and mire, and the Odes and Documents filled pits and traps.
translations.idiomatic: Since the collapse of the late Sui, the schools fell silent, the Confucian Way sank into the mire, and the Odes and Documents were buried in ruin.

sentences.zh: 眷言墳典，每用傷懷。

translations.literal: Turning to the classics of the tombs, each time I am wounded in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of those ancient texts, grief rises in me anew.

sentences.zh: 頃年已來，天下無事，方欲建禮作樂，偃武修文。

translations.literal: In recent years under Heaven there has been no trouble; I am just about to establish rites and make music, lay down arms and cultivate letters.
translations.idiomatic: These last years the realm has been at peace, and I mean to establish ritual and music, to sheathe the sword and revive learning.

sentences.zh: 卿年齒已衰，教將何恃！

translations.literal: Your years and teeth already decline—on whom shall instruction rely!
translations.idiomatic: Yet your years are failing—on whom else can I rely for teaching!

sentences.zh: 所冀才德猶茂，臥振高風，使濟南伏生，重在於茲日；

translations.literal: What I hope is that talent and virtue remain lush, that reclining you still stir noble wind, so that Fusheng of Jinan stands again on this day;
translations.idiomatic: I look to you to keep your talent and virtue in full flower, to uphold a lofty example even in repose, and to make this age see again a Fu Sheng of Jinan;

sentences.zh: 關西孔子，故顯於當今。

translations.literal: the Confucius of Guanxi, thus manifest in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: a Confucius of the west, shining once more in our own time.

sentences.zh: 令問令望，何其美也！

translations.literal: Fine reputation, fine expectation—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Your name and your promise—how splendid they are!

sentences.zh: 念卿疲朽，何以可言！

translations.literal: Thinking of your exhaustion and decay, what can be said!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I think how worn you are, words fail me!

sentences.zh: 尋賜爵封陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ennobled and made Marquis of Yangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ennobled as Marquis of Yang County.

sentences.zh: 十七年，拜秘書少監。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兩宮禮賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Both palaces honored him with gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Both the emperor and the crown prince honored him with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，累表請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he repeatedly petitioned to retire, and at last permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，以師傅恩，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded the throne, out of favor for his role as tutor, he was advanced to Grand Master of the Splendorous Light with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne he advanced Deyan, in gratitude for his service as tutor, to grand master of the splendorous light with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，卒於家，年九十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he died at home, aged ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he died at home, aged ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之輟朝，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: Gaozong suspended court for him and posthumously awarded him Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong suspended court in mourning and posthumously appointed him director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 文集三十卷。

translations.literal: Collected writings, thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 曾孫至忠，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandson Zhizhong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandson Zhizhong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 許叔牙，潤州句容人。

translations.literal: Xu Shuya was a native of Jurong in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuya was a native of Jurong in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少精於《毛詩》、《禮記》，尤善諷詠。

translations.literal: In youth he was expert in the Mao Odes and the Book of Rites, especially skilled at recitation and chanting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he mastered the Mao version of the Odes and the Book of Rites and was especially gifted at recitation.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累授晉王文學兼侍讀，尋遷太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly appointed Literary Attendant to the Prince of Jin and concurrent lecture companion; soon he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was repeatedly appointed literary attendant to the Prince of Jin and reading tutor, and soon afterward became an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 升春宮，加朝散大夫，遷太子洗馬，兼崇賢館學士，仍兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When [the prince] ascended the Eastern Palace, he was given the title Grand Master of Spreading Morality, transferred to Crown Prince Keeper of the Stud, concurrently Chongxian Hall academician, and still concurrently lecture companion.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Shuya was promoted to grand master of spreading morality, made crown prince keeper of the stud, and appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall while retaining his post as reading tutor.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰《毛詩纂義》十卷，以進皇太子。

translations.literal: Once he compiled Exegesis of the Mao Odes in ten juan and presented it to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled Exegesis of the Mao Odes in ten juan and presented it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子賜帛百段，兼令寫本付司經局。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince bestowed one hundred bales of silk and also ordered a fair copy sent to the Classics Office.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rewarded him with one hundred bales of silk and ordered a fair copy deposited with the Office for Classics.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫高智周嘗謂人曰：「凡欲言《詩》者，必須先讀此書。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou once said to others: 'Anyone who wishes to speak of the Odes must first read this book.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Gao Zhizhou once remarked, 'Anyone who means to speak of the Odes must read this book first.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 子子儒。

translations.literal: His son was Ziru.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ziru.

sentences.zh: 子儒，亦以學藝稱。

translations.literal: Ziru, too, was famed for learning and art.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru, too, won renown for scholarship and skill.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，官至天官侍郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During Changshou he reached office as Vice Minister of the Heavenly Office and Hongwen Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era he rose to vice minister of the Heavenly Office and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 子儒居選部，不以藻鑒為意，委令史句直，以為腹心。

translations.literal: When Ziru occupied the Selection Department, he did not take discerning judgment to heart; he entrusted the drafting clerk Gou Zhi and made him his intimate core.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziru headed the Selection Department he paid no attention to judging talent himself, but entrusted everything to the clerk Gou Zhi as his right hand.

sentences.zh: 註官之次，子儒但高枕而臥，時雲「句直平配」。

translations.literal: At the sequence of registering offices, Ziru only slept with a high pillow; the saying went, 'Gou Zhi handles the roster.'
translations.idiomatic: During the registration of appointments Ziru merely lay back with a high pillow, while people said, 'Gou Zhi assigns the posts.'

sentences.zh: 由是補授失序，無復綱紀，道路以為口實。

translations.literal: Because of this appointments fell out of order, discipline was gone, and the roads made it a topic of talk.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments therefore fell into disorder, standards collapsed, and the affair became a byword on the streets.

sentences.zh: 其所註《史記》，竟未就而終。

translations.literal: His commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian in the end was never completed at his death.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian was never finished before he died.

sentences.zh: 敬播，蒲州河東人也。

translations.literal: Jing Bo was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Bo was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 俄有詔詣秘書內省佐顏師古、孔穎達修《隋史》，尋授太子校書。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to the inner Secretariat to assist Yan Shigu and Kong Yingda in compiling the History of Sui; shortly afterward he was appointed Crown Prince collator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict summoned him to the inner Secretariat to assist Yan Shigu and Kong Yingda in compiling the History of Sui, and shortly afterward he was made collator to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 史成，遷著作郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: When the history was completed, he was transferred to Master of Writings and concurrently compiled National History.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was finished he was promoted to master of writings and appointed to help compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 與給事中許敬宗撰《高祖》、《太宗實錄》，自創業至於貞觀十四年，凡四十卷。

translations.literal: With Drafting Gentleman Xu Jingzong he compiled the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong, from founding the enterprise through the fourteenth year of Zhenguan—forty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: Together with drafting gentleman Xu Jingzong he compiled the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong, from the founding of the dynasty down to the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, forty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 奏之，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He presented it and was awarded five hundred segments of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the work and received five hundred segments of goods in reward.

sentences.zh: 太宗之破高麗，名所戰六山為駐蹕，播謂人曰：「聖人者，與天地合德，山名駐蹕，此蓋以鑾輿不復更東矣。」

translations.literal: When Taizong defeated Goguryeo, he named the six mountains where they fought 'Halting the Imperial Carriage.' Bo said to others: 'A sage unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth. To name a mountain "Halting the Carriage"—this surely means the imperial palanquin will not go east again.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong defeated Goguryeo he named the six mountains on which the battles were fought 'Halting the Imperial Carriage.' Bo remarked to others, 'A sage shares the virtue of Heaven and Earth. To call a mountain "Halting the Carriage" can only mean the imperial coach will not travel east again.

sentences.zh: 卒如所言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 時梁國公房玄齡深稱播有良史之才，曰：「陳壽之流也。」

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Liangguo Fang Xuanling deeply praised Bo as having talent for fine history, saying: 'Of the caliber of Chen Shou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke of Liang State Fang Xuanling spoke highly of Bo's gifts as a historian, saying, 'He is of Chen Shou's company.

sentences.zh: 玄齡以顏師古所註《漢書》，文繁難省，令播撮其機要，撰成四十卷，傳於代。

translations.literal: Xuanling, because Yan Shigu's annotated Book of Han was verbose and hard to abridge, ordered Bo to extract its essentials and compile forty juan, transmitted to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yan Shigu's annotated Book of Han too prolix to use easily, Xuanling had Bo distill its essentials into forty juan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 尋以撰實錄功，遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Soon, on the merit of compiling veritable records, he was promoted to Crown Prince Supervisor of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his work on the veritable records, he was promoted to crown prince supervisor of deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時初置此官，極為清望。

translations.literal: At that time this office had just been established; it was extremely prestigious.
translations.idiomatic: The post had only just been created and was regarded as highly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 中書令馬周嘆曰：「所恨資品妄高，不獲歷居此職。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Ma Zhou sighed: 'What I regret is that my qualifications and rank are falsely high; I did not get to hold this post in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat director Ma Zhou sighed, 'What I regret is that my seniority and rank were already too high—I never had the chance to hold that office myself.

sentences.zh: 參撰《晉書》，播與令狐德棻、陽仁卿、李嚴等四人總其類。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Book of Jin; Bo together with Linghu Defen, Yang Renqing, Li Yan, and four others oversaw its categories.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Book of Jin; Bo, together with Linghu Defen, Yang Renqing, Li Yan, and four others, supervised its organization by category.

sentences.zh: 會刑部奏言：「準律：謀反大逆，父子皆坐死，兄弟處流。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of Punishment memorialized: 'According to the law: for treason and great treason, father and son all sit condemned to death; brothers suffer exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Punishment memorialized, 'Under the statute, for treason and great treason father and son alike are put to death, while brothers are exiled,

sentences.zh: 此則輕而不懲，望請改從重法。」

translations.literal: This is lenient without deterrence; we hope to change and follow the severe law.
translations.idiomatic: this is too lenient to deter crime. We ask that the penalty for brothers be made heavier.

sentences.zh: 制遣百僚詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the officials to deliberate fully.

sentences.zh: 播議曰：「昆季孔懷，天倫雖重，比於父子，性理已殊。

translations.literal: Bo argued: 'Between brothers nature's affection runs deep; though heavenly kin is weighty, compared with father and son, nature and principle already differ.
translations.idiomatic: Bo argued, 'Brothers are bound by deep natural affection, yet compared with the tie between father and son their relation is already different in nature and principle.

sentences.zh: 生有異室之文，死有別宗之義。

translations.literal: In life there is the writ of separate chambers; in death the principle of distinct lineages.
translations.idiomatic: In life they belong to separate households; in death they enter different ancestral lines.

sentences.zh: 今有高官重爵，本廕唯逮子孫；

translations.literal: Today for high office and heavy nobility, hereditary entitlement reaches only to sons and grandsons;
translations.idiomatic: Today, when high office and noble rank bring hereditary privilege, that privilege extends only to sons and grandsons;

sentences.zh: 祚土錫珪，余光不及昆季。

translations.literal: when the throne grants land and bestows jade, residual glory does not extend to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: when the throne grants fiefs and bestows jade seals, the reflected honor does not reach brothers.

sentences.zh: 豈有不沾其廕，輒受其辜，背禮違情，殊為太甚！

translations.literal: How could one who does not share their entitlement yet abruptly bear their guilt—contrary to ritual, against feeling—exceedingly excessive!
translations.idiomatic: How then can brothers who share none of that privilege be made to share the guilt? It violates ritual and human feeling alike, and goes too far!

sentences.zh: 必期反茲春令，踵彼秋荼，創次骨於道德之辰，建深文於措刑之日，臣將以為不可。」

translations.literal: If one must reverse this spring ordinance and tread that autumn thistle, plant bone-rending punishment in the season of moral virtue, erect harsh statutes on the day of measured penal action—I regard it as unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: To reverse the leniency of spring and follow the harshness of autumn, to invent punishments that pierce to the bone in an age devoted to virtue, and to pile severe statutes upon a day meant for measured justice—I hold that unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The edict adopted his opinion.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was appointed Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yonghui he was appointed master of writings.

sentences.zh: 與許敬宗等撰《西域圖》。

translations.literal: With Xu Jingzong and others he compiled the Map of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: With Xu Jingzong and others he compiled the Map of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 後歷諫議大夫、給事中，並依舊兼修國史。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Remonstrance Councilor and Drafting Gentleman, in all cases continuing as before to compile National History concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as remonstrance councilor and drafting gentleman, continuing throughout to help compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 又撰《太宗實錄》，從貞觀十五年至二十三年，為二十卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled Taizong's Veritable Records from the fifteenth through the twenty-third year of Zhenguan—twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Taizong's Veritable Records from the fifteenth to the twenty-third year of Zhenguan, twenty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 奏之，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: He presented it and was awarded three hundred bales of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the work and was rewarded with three hundred bales of silk.

sentences.zh: 後坐事出為越州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Later, on account of an offense, he was sent out as chief secretary of the Yuezhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after he was implicated in an offense, he was sent out to serve as chief secretary of the Yuezhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longshuo he died in office.

sentences.zh: 播又著《隋略》二十卷。

translations.literal: Bo also authored Outline of Sui in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also wrote Outline of Sui in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 劉伯莊，徐州彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Bozhuang was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bozhuang was a native of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累除國子助教。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly appointed National University assistant professor.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly appointed assistant professor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 與其舅太學博士侯孝遵齊為弘文館學士，當代榮之。

translations.literal: Together with his maternal uncle, Imperial University erudite Hou Xiaozun, he was appointed Hongwen Hall academician together; the age honored them.
translations.idiomatic: He and his maternal uncle Hou Xiaozun, an erudite of the Imperial University, were appointed together as Hongwen Hall academicians, to the admiration of their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 尋遷國子博士，其後又與許敬宗等參修《文思博要》及《文館詞林》。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Imperial University erudite; afterward again with Xu Jingzong and others he participated in compiling Comprehensive Essentials of Literary Thought and Forest of Phrases from the Literary Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an erudite of the Imperial University, and later joined Xu Jingzong and others in compiling the Comprehensive Essentials of Literary Thought and the Forest of Phrases from the Literary Court.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，兼授崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: During Longshuo he was concurrently appointed Chongxian Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo he was also appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 撰《史記音義》、《史記地名》、《漢書音義》各二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Phonetic Glosses for the Records of the Historian, Place Names for the Records of the Historian, and Phonetic Glosses for the Book of Han—each twenty juan—circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Phonetic Glosses to the Records of the Historian, Place Names in the Records of the Historian, and Phonetic Glosses to the Book of Han, each in twenty juan, and all three circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子之宏，亦傳父業。

translations.literal: His son Zhihong also inherited his father's work.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhihong carried on his father's scholarship.

sentences.zh: 則天時，累遷著作郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's time he was repeatedly promoted to Master of Writings and concurrently compiled National History.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu Zetian he rose through repeated promotions to master of writings and continued to help compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 卒於相王府司馬。

translations.literal: He died as aide of the Prince of Xiang's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as secretary to the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，以故吏贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, as a former subordinate he was posthumously awarded Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong came to the throne he posthumously honored Zhihong, as a former servant, with the title vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秦景通，常州晉陵人也。

translations.literal: Qin Jingtong was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jingtong was a native of Jinling in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與弟肸，尤精《漢書》，當時習《漢書》者皆宗師之，常稱景通為大秦君，暐為小秦君。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Xi, he was especially accomplished in the Book of Han; those who studied the Book of Han at the time all took them as masters, and commonly called Jingtong the Great Lord Qin and Wei the Little Lord Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Xi were especially versed in the Book of Han; everyone who studied that classic in their day looked to them as masters, and people commonly called Jingtong 'Great Lord Qin' and Wei 'Little Lord Qin.'

sentences.zh: 若不經其兄弟指授，則謂之「不經師匠，無足采也」。

translations.literal: If one had not received instruction from the two brothers, they would say, 'Without passing through a master craftsman, it is not worth adopting.'
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who had not studied under the two brothers was dismissed with the saying, 'Without a master's tutelage, it is not worth taking seriously.'

sentences.zh: 景通，貞觀中累遷太子洗馬，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Jingtong, during the Zhenguan era, was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Keeper of the Stud, and concurrently Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan, Jingtong rose through repeated promotions to crown prince keeper of the stud and academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 為《漢書》學者，又有劉納言，亦為當時宗匠。

translations.literal: Among scholars of the Book of Han, there was also Liu Nayin, who likewise was a master of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Another leading scholar of the Book of Han was Liu Nayin, also regarded as a master of his generation.

sentences.zh: 納言，乾封中，歷都水監主簿，以《漢書》授沛王賢。

translations.literal: Nayin, during Qianfeng, served successively as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Waterways, and taught the Book of Han to the Prince of Pei, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianfeng, Nayin served as chief clerk of the Directorate of Waterways and instructed the Prince of Pei, Xian, in the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 及賢為皇太子，累遷太子洗馬，兼充侍讀。

translations.literal: When Xian became Crown Prince, [Nayin] was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Keeper of the Stud, and also appointed lecture companion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was made crown prince, Nayin was promoted to crown prince keeper of the stud and appointed reading tutor.

sentences.zh: 常撰《俳諧集》十五卷，以進太子。

translations.literal: He often compiled fifteen scrolls of the Collection of Jests and presented them to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a fifteen-scroll Collection of Jests and presented it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及東宮廢，高宗見而怒之。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was abolished, Gaozong saw it and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern palace was abolished, Gaozong saw the work and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「劉納言收其余藝，參侍經史，自府入宮，久淹歲月，朝遊夕處，竟無匡贊。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Liu Nayin was retained for his remaining talents to attend upon the classics and histories; from the princely establishment he entered the palace, lingering many months, spending mornings and evenings together, yet in the end contributing no correction or support.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'Liu Nayin was kept on for his miscellaneous skills to serve at the classics and histories. From the prince's household into the palace he went, tarrying month after month in daily company—yet he offered no guidance whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 闕忠孝之良規，進詼諧之鄙說，儲宮敗德，抑有所由。

translations.literal: He lacked good counsel of loyalty and filial piety, and advanced base talk of jest and wit; the crown prince's ruin of virtue also had its cause.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to offer sound counsel in loyalty and filial piety, yet put forward vulgar jests; the heir's moral decay, it would seem, did not arise without cause.

sentences.zh: 情在好生，不忍加戮，宜從屏棄，以勵將來。

translations.literal: Our feeling rests in cherishing life; we cannot bear to add execution; he should be removed and cast aside, to encourage those to come.
translations.idiomatic: Our hearts incline toward sparing life, and we cannot bring ourselves to execute him; let him be cast out instead, as a warning to those who follow.

sentences.zh: 可除名。」

translations.literal: He may be stricken from the roster.'
translations.idiomatic: Let his name be struck from the rolls.'

sentences.zh: 後又坐事配流振州而死。

translations.literal: Later he again, because of an affair, was sentenced to exile in Zhenzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later implicated in another offense, exiled to Zhenzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 羅道琮，蒲州虞鄉人也。

translations.literal: Luo Daocong was a native of Yuxiang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Daocong was a native of Yuxiang in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖順，武德初，為興州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shun, at the beginning of Wude, served as Prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shun served as prefect of Xing Prefecture in the early Wude era.

sentences.zh: 勤於學業，而慷慨有節義。

translations.literal: He was diligent in studies, and generously spirited, possessing integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself diligently to learning and was high-minded, possessed of integrity and principle.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，上書忤旨，配流嶺表。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan, he submitted a memorial that offended the imperial will and was sentenced to exile beyond the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenguan reign he submitted a memorial that displeased the throne and was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 時有同被流者，至荊、襄間病死，臨終，泣謂道琮曰：「人生有死，所恨委骨異壤。」

translations.literal: At that time there was one likewise exiled; reaching the region between Jing and Xiang he died of illness; at the end, weeping, he told Daocong, 'Human life has death; what I regret is leaving my bones in alien soil.'
translations.idiomatic: A fellow exile fell ill and died between Jing and Xiang. On his deathbed he wept and said to Daocong, 'Death comes to us all; what I cannot bear is to leave my bones in a foreign land.'

sentences.zh: 道琮曰：「我若生還，終不獨歸，棄卿於此！」

translations.literal: Daocong said, 'If I return alive, I will never return alone and abandon you here!'
translations.idiomatic: Daocong replied, 'If I make it home alive, I will never return alone and leave you here!'

sentences.zh: 瘞之路左而去。

translations.literal: He buried him by the roadside and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He buried him by the roadside and went on.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遇赦得還，至殯所，屬霖潦瀰漫，柩不復可得。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he encountered an amnesty and was able to return; arriving at the burial place, it happened that flooding rains had spread everywhere, and the coffin could no longer be found.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was pardoned and allowed to return. When he reached the burial site, heavy rains had flooded the area and the coffin was nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 道琮設祭慟哭，告以欲與俱歸之意，若有靈者，幸相警示。

translations.literal: Daocong set out offerings and wept bitterly, telling him of his wish to return together; if there were a spirit, he hoped it would give a sign.
translations.idiomatic: Daocong made offerings and wept aloud, declaring his wish to take the remains home. If his spirit lingered, he prayed, let it show him where they lay.

sentences.zh: 言訖，路側水中，忽然湧沸。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, in the water by the roadside, suddenly it bubbled and boiled up.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he had spoken, the water at the roadside suddenly surged and boiled.

sentences.zh: 道琮又咒云：「若所沸處是，願更令一沸。」

translations.literal: Daocong again incanted, saying, 'If the place that boiled is it, may it boil once more.'
translations.idiomatic: Daocong spoke another prayer: 'If this is the place, let it bubble up once more.'

sentences.zh: 咒訖，又沸。

translations.literal: When the incantation was finished, it boiled again.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, the water bubbled again.

sentences.zh: 道琮便取得其屍，銘誌可驗，遂負之還鄉。

translations.literal: Daocong then obtained his corpse; the inscription could verify it, and he bore it on his back and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Daocong retrieved the body; the inscription on the tomb marker confirmed it, and he shouldered the coffin all the way home.

sentences.zh: 當時識者稱道琮誠感所致。

translations.literal: At the time those who understood praised that it was brought about by Daocong's sincere feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries who witnessed it attributed the marvel to the power of Daocong's sincerity.

sentences.zh: 道琮尋以明經登第。

translations.literal: Before long Daocong, through the Classicist examination, passed and received office.
translations.idiomatic: Daocong soon passed the civil service examination in the Classics specialty.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，官至太學博士。

translations.literal: Near the end of Gaozong's reign, he reached the office of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Gaozong's reign he had risen to erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 每與太學助教康國安、道士李榮等講論，為時所稱。

translations.literal: He often engaged in discourse with Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy Kang Guo'an, the Daoist priest Li Rong, and others, and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly debated learning with the university assistant instructor Kang Guo'an, the Daoist Li Rong, and others, and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.
